aramount/Studio Canal
Sarah Connor’s (Linda Hamilton) lean-yet-ripped physique made her an action heroine on par with Sigourney Weaver’s Ripley in the Alien franchise.
Paramount/Studio Canal
Robert Patrick’s advanced T-1000 makes for a seemingly unbeatable antagonist for the ages.
aramount/Studio Canal
The film also has one of the best villains in cinema with the shapeshifting T-1000 (Robert Patrick). Cameron actually had the idea for a Terminator made of liquid metal when he was writing the first film, but the technology available at the time wasn’t up to the task. Then Cameron made The Abyss in 1989, which featured a flowing, water-like alien at the very end created by Industrial Light & Magic (ILM). ILM made a major investment, expanding its staff and spending over $3 million on new equipment and specially designed software just for Judgment Day.
The gamble paid off. The T-1000 and other visual effects earned critical raves and an Oscar (the film snagged four in all) and helped usher in the golden age of CGI. Audiences loved the character, which had as much to do with Cameron’s expert pacing as the effects. The T-1000’s abilities are only gradually revealed. Initially, the slender Patrick seems no match for Schwarzenegger’s heavily muscled T-800, even if he can take on anyone’s form. Then we see its liquid metal form is impervious to bullet wounds, healing them instantly—even when a gunshot blast splits its head in two. Cameron keeps upping the ante, until one becomes convinced the T-1000 is well-nigh invincible.
“T2 was made for theaters, and our lovingly prepared 3D version, coming back to the big screen, is the absolute best way to see the film,” Cameron told Deadline Hollywood via statement. “I believe it’s safe to do spoilers after 35 years, so SPOILER ALERT: the good guys win against the AI super intelligence. And maybe that’s a message of hope we could use this summer.”
There is a staggered global rollout for the rerelease. It’s now available in Germany, Latin America, the Czech Republic, the US, Italy, and Poland. The film will be released in France on September 2; Australia, New Zealand, the Netherlands, Sweden, and Hungary on September 3; and the United Kingdom on September 4.
And now, we give you 10 of our favorite scenes:
The T-800 in the biker bar
Credit:
Paramount/Studio Canal
Credit:
Paramount/Studio Canal
Judgment Day‘s eye-popping special effects certainly provide plenty of highlights, but Cameron didn’t skimp on the story either. This is a prime example of how the director used touches of levity to make even the film’s more workmanlike segments entertaining. The T-800 arrives from the future naked as a jaybird and must acquire clothing, transportation, and weaponry. Naturally, he wanders into a biker bar—to the delight of the female patrons—finds a dude his size, and demands the biker’s clothes and motorcycle.
The biker thinks it’s a joke at first and refuses, extinguishing his cigar on the T-800’s bared pectoral muscle—with no effect. The outcome of the ensuing bar fight is a given. The T-800 walks away with cool leather clothing, a motorcycle, a shotgun, and a pair of stylish black sunglasses as George Thorogood and the Destroyer’s “Bad to the Bone” plays. The song’s been overused in films since then, but it was the perfect grace note for this scene.
Chase through the aqueduct
Credit:
Paramount/Studio Canal
Credit:
Paramount/Studio Canal
This is the first major chase sequence, with both the T-800 and the T-1000 trying to get to a fleeing John Connor first. John’s little motorbike proves no match for the large truck commandeered by the T-1000, which blasts through a cinder block wall at one point. The T-1000 never falters in its single-minded pursuit, but the arrival of the T-800 saves the boy. The truck eventually explodes, seemingly incinerating the T-1000. It’s only after the T-800 and John ride away that we see the T-1000 emerge from the flames and resume his police officer appearance.
The sequence was filmed over nine hours in LA’s San Fernando Valley. The T-800’s big stunt involved jumping a motorcycle 60 feet (at an altitude of roughly 15 feet) to the flood control channel below. Stunt coordinator Joel Kramer rigged up a support mechanism for the 750-pound motorcycle, since otherwise the jump was deemed too dangerous. The rigging and wires were erased during post-production.
The T-1000 emerges from floor tiles
Credit:
Paramount/Studio Canal
Credit:
Paramount/Studio Canal
This is one of those “upping the ante” moments. We’ve seen the T-1000’s amazing shapeshifting abilities, taking on the form of a policeman and John’s foster mother in quick succession. We’ve seen his arms transform effortlessly into weapons. We’ve seen him heal bullet holes instantly. When he arrives at the psychiatric hospital to take out Sarah Connor, he must briefly hide as a team of detectives exits. A lone security guard goes into the hall to get coffee from the vending machine. The T-1000 is nowhere to be seen—until it slowly oozes up out of the checkerboard hospital floor tiles right behind the unsuspecting guard.
The shot required a special bit of software capable of reshaping specific regions of a 2D image using 3D geometry, mapping a computer-generated replica of the floor to the actual footage. This was combined with animation of the T-1000 taking shape. As for the T-1000 taking on the guard’s shape—that was achieved the old-fashioned way, since the actor Don Stanton had a twin brother (Dan).
“Come with me if you want to live”
Credit:
aramount/Studio Canal
Credit:
aramount/Studio Canal
This is where flipping the script to make the T-800 John’s protector instead of the hunter really pays emotional dividends. Sarah Connor has reshaped her entire persona (not just her physique) in the wake of what happened to her in the first film. Everything centers on protecting John from the machines. Her obsession gets her locked up in a psychiatric hospital, and her odds of release are not good.
She’s in the middle of breaking out on her own—quite effectively—and has made it to the elevator, which opens to reveal the T-800, her former adversary, back (in her mind) to kill her and John. Horrified, Sarah flees back the way she came and is briefly subdued by hospital staff until the T-800 tosses them aside like rag dolls. She sees John is safe, and the T-800 reaches down and repeats the line her protector uttered in the first film: “Come with me if you want to live.”
Bonus: Sarah’s psychiatrist and everyone else who thought she was crazy rattling on about killer machines from the future must confront the fact that she was right all along, especially when the T-1000 shows up.
Sarah’s nuclear holocaust dream
Paramount/Studio Canal
Paramount/Studio Canal
Paramount/Studio Canal
Paramount/Studio Canal
Paramount/Studio Canal
Paramount/Studio Canal
This powerful dream sequence shows Sarah and the rest of Los Angeles utterly annihilated by a nuclear blast. It starts with children and their mothers—including a younger, more innocent Sarah Connor—on a playground, oblivious to the danger, as a distraught Sarah soundlessly tries to warn them by banging on the chain-link fence. Then the blast hits, burning Sarah alive (actually a full-sized puppet) and reducing those children to ash.
It took a ton of special effects work to pull off the sequence, combining practical effects, miniatures, and CGI enhancements. The team built a mini-Los Angeles based on the live-action footage, including skyscrapers and an overpass. Some of the model buildings stood 5 feet tall, and many were designed to break away to mimic the effects of a blast. The nuclear fireball was actually a backlit, 8-foot plexiglass column. The most powerful visual effect is the ashy remains of the playground victims, still intact—until a shock wave scatters the ashes to the wind.
That arm scene
Credit:
aramount/Studio Canal
Credit:
aramount/Studio Canal
Sarah’s dream is sufficiently traumatic to compel her to leave John with the T-800 and seek out Miles Dyson (Joe Morton), Cyberdyne’s director of special projects and the scientist most responsible for developing what would become Skynet. Her plan is to kill Miles and stop Judgment Day from ever happening—hence the film’s catchphrase, “No fate but what we make.” But she can’t go through with it, even as John and the T-800 arrive to stop her.
To prove to Miles that Sarah is telling the truth—that his work will lead to humanity’s near-annihilation—the T-800 removes the skin from his hand and forearm, revealing the cyber skeleton underneath. As he flexes the mechanical fingers in front of a horrified Miles and his wife, the T-800 intones, “Now listen to me very carefully….” I’m sure Miles was hanging on his every word.
The Cyberdyne showdown
Credit:
aramount/Studio Canal
Credit:
aramount/Studio Canal
John, Sarah, and the T-800 enlist Miles’ help to break into Cyberdyne headquarters and steal the salvaged arm and computer chip left behind by the T-800 in the first film. They are working against the clock, since pretty much every law enforcement unit in the city arrives at the building to stop them. John’s hacking skills prove useful, as does the T-800’s extensive firepower—although per John’s instructions, there are zero human fatalities.
Ultimately, Miles sacrifices himself so that the others can escape, holding onto the detonator that sets off a massive explosion until his final breath. The filming site was an empty office building in Fremont, California, and the explosion was real; pyrotechnician Tom Fisher used hundreds of gallons of gas to create that giant fireball. Respect.
T-1000 vs. liquid nitrogen
Paramount/Studio Canal
Paramount/Studio Canal
Paramount/Studio Canal
Paramount/Studio Canal
Paramount/Studio Canal
Paramount/Studio Canal
The carefully orchestrated high-speed chase down a highway that immediately precedes this scene deserves its own spot on the list, just for the ingenuity of the stunt design. That chase ends with a semitruck pulling a tank of liquid nitrogen overturning and skidding into an active steel mill, spilling liquid nitrogen all over the street. The T-1000 resolutely wades toward its targets anyway, only to start to freeze from the feet up, breaking its legs off at the knees and losing a hand before it solidifies, a look of shocked surprise on its face. The T-800 blasts it to smithereens with a well-timed, “Hasta la vista, baby.”
That should be the end of the T-1000, right? RIGHT? But within minutes the scattered shards start to melt in the heat of the steel mill and begin to coalesce yet again. “We don’t have much time,” the T-800 observes—and indeed, the T-1000 soon reassembles. The frozen shards were actually made of serabin, a material used as ballast for model railroad cars that resembles chrome when it’s polished. Frozen mercury didn’t work because it turned white. But globs of liquid mercury worked just fine to show the melting shards coming together, even though its toxicity meant the special effects crew had to wear protective gear over the two-day shoot.
The T-1000 has a meltdown
Spoiler alert: The T-1000 is not quite unbeatable. Sure, he recovers nicely from a hole in the head, courtesy of Sarah, and being cleaved in two by the T-800 wielding a piece of rebar—the former achieved with a mechanical head and shoulders replica of Patrick (“Donut Head”), the latter with a maquette sculpture (“Cleave Man”), both augmented with CGI. Just when things are looking dire for John and Sarah, the T-800 reboots on auxiliary power and shoots the T-1000 with a grenade launcher. The torso explodes and creates “Pretzel Man” (achieved with three full-sized puppets).
A teetering T-1000 then topples into a vat of molten steel and slowly melts into oblivion, running through each of the human forms it took on over the course of the film (foster mom, security guard, etc.) before vanishing in a howl. This was the most difficult sequence for the special effects team and took weeks to complete, matching carefully choreographed movements of all the actors in the live-action pit with splashing liquid filmed in a separate miniature version of the vat. The illusion of molten steel was basically water and mineral oil mixed with a little powdered sugar; creative lighting and heaters placed below the cameras—plus a few CGI sparks in the background—did the rest.
The result didn’t quite satisfy Cameron, but the rendering shots took so long that the director ran out of time, even with the production crew working 24-hour shifts. The final print wasn’t delivered to theaters until the night before the official release. But audiences were blown away. It was the perfect way to bring about the T-1000’s demise.
The T-800’s final sacrifice
Credit:
Paramount/Studio Canal
Credit:
Paramount/Studio Canal
After that spectacular special effects achievement, Cameron closed things out with an emotional, well-earned farewell. John drops the first T-800 arm and chip into the vat of molten steel to destroy them. But there is one chip left: the one in the new T-800’s head. Since it cannot self-terminate, Sarah is tasked with lowering the machine into the vat, against John’s anguished objections. It’s the final payoff to the relationship Cameron has painstakingly built between John and the machine—and the T-800 goes out in style, giving a gloved thumbs-up as its hand slowly sinks into the liquid steel.
Jennifer is a senior writer at Ars Technica with a particular focus on where science meets culture, covering everything from physics and related interdisciplinary topics to her favorite films and TV series. Jennifer lives in Baltimore with her spouse, physicist Sean M. Carroll, and their two cats, Ariel and Caliban.

articles.title: Canada's counter tariffs hit phones, game consoles -- but don't worry
articles.text:
Canada will soon apply new tariffs on U.S. goods amid the ongoing trade war, including tech like phones. But that likely won’t mean your next iPhone will cost more — at least, it won’t be because of tariffs.
Starting Sept. 8, 2026, Canada’s counter tariffs will come into effect for tons of U.S. goods in response to tariffs the U.S. placed on Canadian goods in President Donald Trump’s inane trade war. Canada’s retaliatory tariffs will focus on sectors most impacted by U.S. tariffs, including steel, dairy, appliances, and more. Crucially for us in the tech world, electronics are also getting hit by tariffs.
A list of Canada’s counter tariffs published (and updated) this week includes items like phones, game consoles, monitors and projectors at the 50 per cent tariff rate. But don’t panic — Canadians probably don’t need to worry about already-pricey electronics getting even more expensive. At least, not because of tariffs.
“What I would say to most Canadians is, don’t be too worried that suddenly [you’re] going to see 50 per cent price hikes,” said Kevin Jia, co-founder and CEO of Canadian custom PC builder Quoted Tech, in an interview with MobileSyrup. “If somebody is telling you, ‘hey, by the way, this is 50 per cent more expensive because of the tariffs,’ I would question that.”
All about the country of origin
The key factor with tariffs is the country of origin, and how governments determine the country of origin will impact what does and doesn’t get tariffed. Canada’s counter tariffs specifically apply to goods “originating from the U.S.,” but with the fluidity of the situation and the size of the policy, it’s not immediately clear what will and won’t count as originating in the U.S.
“I think people often get very confused with how tariffs work. Really what it hinges on is whether something is treated as the country of origin of where that product comes from,” Jia explained.
Jia went on to use his own company, Quoted, as an example, explaining that while most of the assembly work is done in Canada, when the company ships products to the U.S., they’re treated as originating from Vietnam instead of Canada. Why? Because that’s where the CPU is assembled, and the soldering work is completed. Jia says the U.S. considers that work as the “critical transformation of the product,” and because it happens in Vietnam, that country is considered the origin of the goods.
“The question is, ‘where is the country of origin,’ and I think the vast majority of products, especially in gaming and consoles, are not the country of origin in Canada or the United States, despite the fact that there’s assembly work that happens in these two countries,” Jia said.
Mistakes are likely
However, Jia also acknowledged that things are still being finalized and much is still up in the air. Ultimately, it will come down to practical enforcement.
“These are major, major policy shifts that happen very quickly, and agencies just kind of scramble,” Jia said. “The tariff book is massive… there are millions of tariff codes, and they’re all wrapped up together. It can be hopelessly confusing as a business, let alone an individual consumer.”
And that’s not even getting into the potential for errors, which Jia notes can happen often. Agencies can make mistakes, misinterpret a rule, or a business can misdeclare something, which together can create chaos.
MobileSyrup also reached out to Apple, Google, and Xbox about the tariffs. Neither Apple nor Xbox responded before publication, while Google said it didn’t have anything to share about the potential tariff impact on its products.
Real price pressure comes from AI
But while Canadians might not need to worry about tariffs spiking the cost of their next iPhone, there are other issues putting more pressure on tech costs.
“Right now, the bigger problem is chip-flation because of AI datacentres,” Jia said. “That’s going to cause a major, major price — more than anything the tariffs can cause truthfully — on the actual movement of pricing.”
When it comes to avoiding rising costs, Jia advised Canadians should only buy tech when they need to. But if you are looking to get something, right now, sooner is better than later because of chip-flation.

articles.title: Cloudflare frees up 100TB of RAM by shrinking 1.1.1.1's DNS cache entries — 250 billion cached DNS entries at any given time means one wasted byte costs 250GB
articles.text:
Cloudflare frees up 100TB of RAM by shrinking 1.1.1.1's DNS cache entries — 250 billion cached DNS entries at any given time means one wasted byte costs 250GB
Per-entry memory cut by 56%, sparing Cloudflare 130 Gen 13 servers’ worth of DDR5.
Cloudflare says that it has freed up roughly 100TB of RAM across its global fleet without reconfiguring any physical RAM modules in its servers, and that it did so by redesigning how each DNS cache entry is laid out in memory. In a technical blog post, systems engineer Sebastiaan Neuteboom gave us an in-depth look at five Rust-level changes to Big Pineapple, the platform behind the 1.1.1.1 resolver, that shrank each cached entry from 953 bytes to 420 bytes and made the cache faster in the process, with insert throughput up 43% and lookup latency down 19%. The recovered memory matches the combined DDR5 in 130 of Cloudflare's 768GB Gen 13 servers, reclaimed in the face of server-grade DDR5 prices that are on track to double year over year.
Just one wasted byte per entry costs Cloudflare more than 250GB of fleet memory, which is a consequence of Big Pineapple holding more than “250 billion cached DNS entries at any given time.” The first of the five changes, replacing Rust's growable Vec and String containers with fixed-size boxed slices, saved over 15TB on its own by dropping capacity fields the data never uses once cached.
Further changes collapsed the three record lists in every DNS response into one buffer indexed by 2-byte offsets, and dropped owner names that duplicate the queried domain, rebuilding them at read time instead. The last change stores record data as length-prefixed raw wire-format bytes, ending an arrangement in which a 4-byte A record took up the same 144 bytes as the largest record type Cloudflare caches, the rarely seen NAPTR.
Packing record data contiguously also improved CPU cache locality, meaning that most record types now copy straight from the stored buffer into outgoing responses instead of being re-serialized field by field.
According to Cloudflare’s benchmarks in the technical blog, insert throughput is now 893,000 entries per second, up from 625,000, with lookup latency down from 828 to 670 nanoseconds. Over the rollout, which ran from mid-May to early July, p99 resident memory per instance fell from 9.3GB to 5.3GB.
The Gen 13 servers, which Cloudflare calls its most powerful yet, each carry 768GB of DDR5-6400. The company settled on that config back in March after pricing out a 1,152GB option and rejecting it partly because of high memory prices.
This DNS cache work is the second large memory-reclamation project Cloudflare has completed in the last year, following the FL2 rewrite of its request-handling layer in Rust last September. Efficiency has been driving the company’s hardware picks for years, including the switch to AMD's 96-core EPYC 9684X for its Gen 12 servers.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
None of the liberated RAM will be cashed out as smaller memory configurations, though; Cloudflare plans to pour it back into larger DNS caches, which raise hit rates and cut the query traffic it sends upstream to authoritative servers.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Luke James is a freelance writer and journalist. Although his background is in legal, he has a personal interest in all things tech, especially hardware and microelectronics, and anything regulatory.

Just for DNS, just in memory costs.Reply

We've had so much surplus memory it was cheaper to code less and cache more to pretend like systems and apps were more performant than they actually were. Just relying on caching everything they need to do the work quickly, rather than coding it to work smart and efficiently.Reply

articles.title: Von Commodore bis Kassetten: Diese 8 Gadgets bringen Retro-Feeling zurück
articles.text:
Von Commodore bis Kassetten: 8 moderne Gadgets mit echtem Retro-Charme
Nein, früher war sicherlich nicht alles besser. Aber einiges eben doch. Zum Beispiel die CD-Sammlung, die man behutsam kuratiert und wertgeschätzt hat, statt unaufmerksam eine randomisierte Streaming-Playlist im Hintergrund laufen zu lassen. Oder die ersten Handys, mit denen man tatsächlich noch telefoniert hat und nicht nur stundenlang durch Social Media gescrollt ist.
Zumindest lösen diese und andere Erinnerungen bei vielen Menschen eine große Sehnsucht aus. Und wenn man die Zeit auch nicht zurückholen kann, so doch zumindest ein paar der Gegenstände, die einem damals so wichtig waren – wenn auch in moderner Form. Diese acht Gadgets setzen ganz auf Nostalgie.
CD-Player im Fotoformat
Mit den CD-Playern früherer Tage hat die Variante der japanischen Firma KM5 nur noch wenig gemein. Hier ist der Player kaum noch größer als die CD selbst. Das quadratische Sichtfenster ist von einem Rahmen umgeben, der an den Seiten schmal und unten größer ist. Das erinnert an das Fotoformat von Instantkameras. Das Sichtfenster lässt sich mit einem CD-Cover überdecken. Preis: 180 Euro
Anruf aus der Vergangenheit
Mit dem C64 und Amiga hat Commodore die frühe PC-Landschaft geprägt. Nun versucht sich das 2025 wiederbelebte Unternehmen an einem sogenannten Dumbphone: Das Commodore Callback ist ein Klapphandy, das zwar Apps für Messaging, Musikstreaming und Navigation unterstützt. Social-Media-Apps und Browser sind aber gesperrt. Getippt wird auf einem klassischen Ziffernblock mit T9-Wörterbuch. Preis: ab 399 US-Dollar.
Wackel-Gif auf Fotofilm
Mit dem Aufkommen von Digitalkameras sind Kameras mit Fotofilmen praktisch verschwunden. Das Unternehmen Reto stellt sich gegen den Trend – und setzt weiterhin auf die analoge Technik. Die Reto 3D Classic hat zusätzlich einen Twist verbaut. Die drei Linsen schießen vom selben Motiv drei Hochkant-Fotos in leicht versetzter Perspektive. Auf der Filmrolle werden dafür anderthalb Plätze verbraucht. Die zugehörige App erstellt aus den drei Analogfotos, die vorher eingescannt werden müssen, ein animiertes Gif mit einem 3D-Wackel-Effekt. Preis: 79,20 Dollar.
Smartwatch im Casio-Pelz
Casio-Uhren gelten als Designklassiker – besonders smart sind sie nach heutigen Maßstäben aber nicht. Ollee Watch möchte das ändern. Das Startup hat ein Nachrüst-Kit entwickelt, dank der die Uhren neben der Zeit auch Temperatur und Herzfrequenz sowie gegangene Schritte messen können. Dafür wird ein neuer Chip eingesetzt. Daten werden dann per Bluetooth ans Smartphone gesendet. Die Batterie der Uhr soll bis zu zehn Monate durchhalten. Preis: ab 54,99 Dollar.
Spaciger Screen
Die 1970 erschienene Videosphere ist ein ulkiges Produkt der Tech-Geschichte. Der kugelförmige Röhrenfernseher der Marke JVC erinnert optisch an einen Astronautenhelm. Die Firma Iretro Lab hat die Gehäuseform per 3D-Druck kopiert – setzt aber auf ein modernes Innenleben mit Retina-Displays aus iPads. Per USB-C können Computer angeschlossen werden, ein Mac Mini kann im Gehäuse verstaut werden. Im Gerätefuß ist eine mechanische Flip-Uhr verbaut. Preis: 769,99 Dollar.
Diskette mit Haltung
Als Speichermedium haben Disketten wegen ihrer geringen Kapazität längst ausgedient, als Icon für die Speicherfunktion bei Software haben sie aber überlebt. Das Unternehmen Wakcas bedient sich an dem ikonischen Design für einen iPhone-Ständer. Das Gadget ist Mag-Safe-kompatibel und haftet an der Rückseite des iOS-Geräts. Zum Abstellen wird die Halter-Diskette in der Mitte aufgeklappt. Die Firma hat zudem optisch passende Hüllen im Programm. Preis: 35,95 Euro.
Alles im ZIP-Ordner
Das Modelabel Forever Vacation hat mit in.tern.et noch einen zweiten Online-Store, der um einiges unbekannter ist. Hier tummeln sich allerlei Klamotten, Poster und Schmuck in einer Retro-Internet-Ästhetik. Zu finden ist hier etwa eine Kollaboration mit WinRar. Neben T-Shirts und Hoodies gibt es auch eine ZIP-Ordner-Tasche aus veganem Leder, die dem Logo nachempfunden ist. Preis: 115 Euro
Spul das Tape zurück
Das Unternehmen We are Rewind hat sich zur Aufgabe gemacht, Kassettenspieler und Blaster wieder cool zu machen. Wie das klappen soll? Mit knalligen Farben und Kooperationen mit großen Namen. Mit dem US-Rapper Ab-Soul oder dem Videospiel Fortnite hat We are Rewind schon gemeinsame Kassettenspieler veröffentlicht. Momentan gibt es eine limitierte Koop mit den Markenverwertern von Elvis Presley – dazu gehört sein ´68er Comeback-Special. Preis: 179 Euro
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 20.08.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.

articles.title: Brave's browser one-ups Chrome with its new support for email aliases | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Chrome alternative Brave just added a good reason to make the switch to its browser: email aliases. The feature, announced this week, allows Brave’s users to sign up for websites and other online services without having to share their personal email addresses.
To use the feature, you first need to create an account with Brave, where you can provide your real email address. Then, once logged into the browser, you’ll see a pop-up appear when clicking an email field on a website, offering the option to use an alias instead. (If the pop-up doesn’t appear, just right-click on the field to access the option.) The email alias will be filled in on the website’s form, and any emails coming to that address will be forwarded to your primary email account.
The company explains that using an alias can protect your privacy, particularly because websites use your email as a personal identifier, allowing them to target you for ads. Ad tech giants like Meta are also able to match the email you provided to a retailer’s website, for instance, with the address they have on file for you, allowing these companies to track what you bought or viewed.
Plus, if any website where you shared your email gets hacked, the hackers will then know your primary email address, and this information can be leaked and shared with data brokers.
Brave says it built the new feature to plug this privacy hole, adding that it doesn’t read the contents of emails sent to an alias — it only processes them for spam and virus filtering. After the email is forwarded, Brave deletes it from its servers. All data in users’ Brave accounts is also encrypted at rest, and any notes you save alongside an alias are stored locally on your device, unless you turn on the sync option. If syncing is enabled, notes will be encrypted end-to-end.
As the email alias feature is still new, Brave cautioned that some of the forwarded mail may initially go to your spam folder, but this should improve as Brave builds up its reputation score as a mail provider.
For the time being, Brave users are being offered five free email aliases. More will be available for Premium plan users in the future.

articles.title: C'est fou ! Anthropic dépasse SpaceX et devient le favori de la plus grosse entrée en Bourse de 2026
articles.text:
Anthropic pourrait bien voler la vedette à SpaceX avant même son entrée en Bourse. Sur les marchés de prédiction, les paris penchent désormais en faveur du créateur de Claude pour la plus importante entrée en Bourse de l’année. Les chiffres donnent le tournis.
Au mois de juin, SpaceX a marqué l’histoire des marchés avec son introduction (IPO) record. Le géant spatial d’Elon Musk a en effet levé 86 milliards de dollars, de quoi porter sa valorisation à 1 770 milliards de dollars. Des chiffres qui semblaient clairement indétrônables. Mais Anthropic pourrait bien, elle aussi, faire exploser les compteurs.
Car sur Polymarket, les traders estiment désormais que son entrée en Bourse, qui devrait se produire aux alentours d’octobre, surpassera celle de son homologue.
Valorisation à 2 000 milliards ?
Ces nouvelles prédictions font suite à l’annonce, par le Wall Street Journal, qu’Anthropic s’apprête à annoncer à ses futurs investisseurs un marché potentiel total supérieur à 30 000 milliards de dollars. SpaceX revendiquait 28 500 milliards de dollars lors de son IPO.
Cet indice, surnommé TAM, sert aux entreprises à démontrer, chiffres à l’appui, l’ampleur du marché qu’elles pourraient théoriquement conquérir. Un exercice toujours approximatif poussé à des sommets inédits par l’intelligence artificielle (IA). À titre de comparaison, Uber évoquait 6 000 milliards de dollars lors de son entrée en Bourse en 2019.
Ainsi, Anthropic viserait une levée de fonds pouvant atteindre les 100 milliards de dollars, pour une capitalisation autour de 2 000 milliards de dollars. Il s’agirait, quelques mois après SpaceX, de l’IPO la plus importante de l’Histoire.
- Upload de fichiers pouvant aller jusqu'à 100 000 tokens (75 000 mots environ)
- Personnalisation avancée
- Conception éthique
La folie de l’IA ne s’estompe pas
Mais ce n’est pas tout. Car le créateur de Claude projette environ 200 milliards de dollars de revenus en 2028, tandis que son chiffre d’affaires a plus que doublé au deuxième trimestre pour s’établir à 11,6 milliards de dollars. Cette trajectoire hors normes illustre l’engouement sans précédent autour de l’IA.
En amont, OpenAI prépare elle aussi son entrée en Bourse, avec une valorisation qui pourrait dépasser les 1 000 milliards de dollars. L’industrie carbure désormais à des chiffres qui semblaient inimaginables il y a encore quelques années. Preuve en est : NVIDIA, pierre angulaire de l’écosystème, prévoit 70 % de croissance de son chiffre d’affaires l’année prochaine.
Toutefois, ces paris comportent leur part de risque. Mais les investisseurs semblent bel et bien décidés à en prendre.
Le TAM (marché adressable total) estime la taille maximale du marché qu’une entreprise pourrait viser si elle captait théoriquement 100 % de la demande. C’est un indicateur utilisé dans les présentations aux investisseurs pour justifier un potentiel de croissance, surtout quand l’activité actuelle est encore en phase d’expansion. Le chiffre dépend fortement des hypothèses (périmètre retenu, prix futurs, taux d’adoption, segments inclus), ce qui le rend très variable d’un acteur à l’autre. Dans l’IA, le TAM a tendance à gonfler car la technologie peut s’appliquer à de nombreux secteurs, mais cela ne garantit ni des revenus, ni une part de marché réaliste.
Un marché de prédiction permet d’acheter et de vendre des contrats indexés sur un événement futur (par exemple, « telle entreprise fera la plus grosse IPO de l’année »). Le prix d’un contrat reflète l’équilibre offre/demande entre participants, et est souvent interprété comme une probabilité, sans être une mesure scientifique. Cette « probabilité » agrège surtout des informations publiques, des anticipations et parfois des biais spéculatifs des traders. La liquidité du marché, les limites de mise et la définition exacte de l’événement (conditions, dates, sources de référence) influencent fortement le signal.
La levée de fonds correspond à l’argent effectivement collecté en vendant des actions nouvelles (ou parfois via des ventes d’actions existantes), et sert à financer l’entreprise ou à offrir de la liquidité à certains actionnaires. La valorisation est l’estimation de la valeur totale de l’entreprise à un instant donné, souvent déduite du prix par action et du nombre total d’actions. La capitalisation boursière est la valorisation telle qu’elle ressort du marché une fois l’action cotée (prix de marché × nombre d’actions), et elle peut varier fortement après l’introduction. En pratique, une très grosse valorisation n’implique pas forcément une levée de fonds équivalente : on peut être valorisé très haut tout en ne vendant qu’une petite fraction du capital au moment de l’IPO.

articles.title: On a essayé les combats de Fable, et ils sont efficaces
articles.text:
Il ne fait aucun doute que Microsoft, plus particulièrement sa branche Xbox, joue gros avec Fable — reboot d’une saga culte de RPG. La multinationale l’a d’ailleurs encore repoussé pour lui donner les meilleures chances. Autrefois attendu pour cette fin d’année, le titre développé par Playground Games est désormais attendu pour le 23 février 2027.
À quelques mois de cette échéance attendue de pied ferme par une horde de fans, Fable était pour la première fois jouable lors de la Gamescom 2026. Microsoft a convié une poignée de journalistes à essayer le RPG le temps d’une démo axée sur un point crucial : les combats. J’ai donc pu essayer le titre pendant plusieurs dizaines de minutes, et je suis assez convaincu des sensations alors que je craignais le pire sur le plan de l’action.
Fable rassure sur ses combats
Il y a en effet toujours à redire sur les affrontements dans les RPG occidentaux ambitieux. Ceux de The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt ? On préfère les oublier et souligner d’autres qualités. Ceux de The Blood of Dawnwalker ? Il y a l’ombre d’un doute, d’après nos premières impressions. Bref, ce n’est pas toujours la fête de ce point de vue, et Fable se devait de rassurer sur l’un des éléments phares de l’aventure qu’on nous promet grandiose.
L’aperçu proposé par Microsoft se découpait en deux temps, sachant qu’on rejouait la même phase, avec simplement un équipement différent. Le but de Playground Games était de nous faire comprendre les multiples possibilités qui s’offrent à nous quand il s’agit d’éliminer la vermine — en l’occurrence, ici, une horde de squelettes animés par des esprits, jusqu’à un mini-boss aérien.
Notez d’ailleurs qu’il n’était aucunement question de s’émerveiller sur la direction artistique, puisque les environnements étaient sombres (une grotte, puis une forêt inquiétante). Ni sur la partie graphique, les développeurs ayant fait le choix assumé de nous faire jouer à un rendu avec des paramètres moyens pour mettre en avant l’optimisation. C’est louable, d’autant que le rendu était suffisamment beau pour ne pas tiquer.
Du coup, ça donne quoi, Fable, avec une manette entre les mains ? Disons que le RPG ne se prend pas pour un autre, avec un gameplay qui mise moins sur la complexité que sur l’efficacité. Les sensations sont globalement bonnes, avec une fluidité bienvenue qui rend l’expérience dynamique. Concrètement, notre héros, qui se battait avec un gros marteau dans les deux portions, a à sa disposition une palette de sorts variés, sachant que leur utilisation n’est pas indexée sur une jauge de mana. Chacun dispose d’un rechargement qui prend plus ou moins de temps, et c’est à la joueuse ou au joueur de bien piocher dans son arsenal pour s’en sortir, en fonction de la manière dont évolue la situation.
Pêle-mêle, on a pu découvrir une boule de feu et un éclair particulièrement puissants ; un sort de poussée utile quand il y a plusieurs ennemis en face de soi ; un pouvoir d’élévation puis d’écrasement assez grisant à l’usage ; ou encore la possibilité de transformer ses adversaires en… poulet. À cela s’ajoute une arme à distance, à savoir un arc (démo 1) ou une arbalète (démo 2) — qui se recharge seule elle aussi. Vous l’aurez compris, Fable mise sur la polyvalence pour plaire un maximum, et c’est fonctionnel, sans être pénible. Ce n’est pas une petite victoire, et on se demande juste ce qu’il en sera à la longue et si le défi sera à la hauteur. À ce sujet, plusieurs options de difficulté sont proposées, avec même des réglages hyper fins sur certains paramètres (dégâts ennemis…).
Dit autrement, Playground Games a compris qu’il est nécessaire de montrer cette facette de Fable pour pouvoir évacuer l’une des craintes qui entourent ce projet de longue date. Le retour dans le royaume d’Albion pourrait bien être triomphant.

articles.title: Meta’s India, Southeast Asia VP Sandhya Devanathan moves to OpenAI
articles.text:
Meta’s India, Southeast Asia VP Sandhya Devanathan moves to OpenAI
Devanathan will join OpenAI as Vice President for Southeast Asia and Australia in October, overseeing consumer growth, enterprise adoption, partnerships, regulatory engagement and operations.
Sandhya Devanathan, Meta’s Vice President for India and Southeast Asia, is leaving the social media giant after more than a decade to join OpenAI.
Devanathan will take over as Vice President for Southeast Asia and Australia at OpenAI in October. Based in Singapore, she will report to Kiran Mani, OpenAI’s Managing Director for Asia-Pacific. The newly created role will see her oversee consumer growth, enterprise adoption and partnerships, regulatory engagement and operations across the region, according to reports.
Devanathan announced her departure from Meta in a LinkedIn post on Friday, although she did not disclose her next employer.
“After more than a decade at Meta, I’ve made the bittersweet decision to move on to my next adventure,” she wrote, adding that she would take a short break before starting her next chapter.
Decade-long career at Meta
She joined Meta in 2016, when the company had around 300 employees in Singapore. Over the next decade, Devanathan worked across ecommerce and gaming in Asia-Pacific, helped build Meta’s businesses in Singapore and Vietnam, and worked on its ecommerce initiatives across Southeast Asia.
In 2020, she took charge of Meta’s gaming business in Asia-Pacific. She was appointed Vice President and Head of Meta India in late 2022 and formally moved into the role in January 2023, with responsibility for the company’s business and revenue priorities in one of its largest markets.
Her mandate was subsequently expanded to include Southeast Asia.
Reflecting on her tenure, Devanathan pointed to the growth of businesses and digital services built around Meta’s platforms across the region, including government citizen services delivered through WhatsApp in India and small businesses using Meta’s apps as digital storefronts in Vietnam, Indonesia and Thailand.
OpenAI’s regional expansion
Her move comes as OpenAI steps up its expansion across Asia-Pacific. The ChatGPT maker has opened offices in markets including Singapore, Tokyo, Seoul, Sydney and Delhi over the past two years. Devanathan will be OpenAI’s most senior executive covering Southeast Asia and Australia, with a remit that also includes building partnerships with businesses, institutions and governments.
OpenAI has also been strengthening its India leadership. In June, it appointed former Uber India and South Asia President Prabhjeet Singh as Managing Director for India.
At Meta, Arun Srinivas, who was appointed Managing Director and Country Head for India in 2025, is expected to continue leading the India business. Benjamin Joe, Meta’s Regional Vice President for Asia-Pacific, said in a comment on Devanathan’s LinkedIn post that Srinivas would join his leadership team and “take Meta India forward”.

articles.title: Pourquoi Nvidia fabrique sa propre mémoire IA : le NVHBM — Frandroid
articles.text:
Jusqu’ici, la mémoire haute performance des accélérateurs IA, la fameuse HBM empilée en petites tours, venait de trois fabricants : SK Hynix, Samsung et Micron. Le contrôleur qui la pilote, lui, vivait sur la puce du processeur.
Nvidia vient de le déplacer directement à l’intérieur de la pile mémoire. Ce déménagement ressemble à un détail de plomberie interne, c’est en réalité un changement d’architecture. C’est ce qui s’appelle la HBM4E.
L’IA générative crée du contenu en quelques secondes, mais souvent au prix de vos données personnelles. Avec Lumo AI, l’assistant européen de Proton, vos conversations restent 100 % confidentielles.
Pour ceux qui ont loupé la première brique, la HBM (pour High Bandwidth Memory), c’est cette mémoire ultra-rapide réservée aux puces IA, faite de plusieurs galettes de silicium empilées et reliées à la verticale pour multiplier le débit. La HBM4 en est la génération la plus récente, celle que se disputent aujourd’hui les fabricants d’accélérateurs. Plus la mémoire va vite, plus le processeur peut être nourri en données sans jamais tourner à vide.
Nvidia revendique de beaux gains face au HBM4E, la prochaine génération du standard mémoire : jusqu’à 30 % de bande passante en plus et 15 % de consommation en moins. Rapprocher le contrôleur des cellules mémoire raccourcit le trajet des données et réduit la latence. L’interface plus compacte libère au passage jusqu’à 25 % de surface sur la puce de calcul, que Nvidia peut remplir de cœurs supplémentaires. Pour entraîner ou faire tourner un grand modèle, le frein vient rarement de la puissance brute. Il vient du débit entre la mémoire et le processeur.
Amazon en cobaye de luxe
Le premier à l’utiliser, c’est justement Amazon, avec son processeur IA Trainium4. La mémoire a d’ailleurs été mise au point avec Annapurna Labs, la division puces maison du groupe.
Les deux entreprises ont annoncé le déploiement de 2 millions de GPU supplémentaires entre 2027 et 2028, avec les processeurs Vera et cette mémoire NVHBM. Le calendrier tombe en pleine crise de la mémoire, où toute la capacité de production 2027 est déjà vendue, et où les prix de la RAM s’envolent.
En logeant son contrôleur dans la pile, Nvidia récupère une couche jusqu’ici laissée à ses fournisseurs mémoire. Sa disponibilité dans les GPU grand public, elle, reste inconnue.
Pour un fabricant qui a déjà relevé trois fois le prix de ses cartes cette année et qui lorgne des pépites comme Hugging Face, verrouiller un maillon de plus n’a rien d’étonnant.

articles.title: Javier Bardem ha dicho que en su casa uno de los dos siempre está con los niños. La ciencia lleva 60 años discutiendo si eso es bueno
articles.text:
"En nuestra casa hay algo innegociable: que al menos uno de los dos debe estar siempre con ellos". Lo decía Javier Bardem en una entrevista en la que promocionaba 'El ser querido', la película de Rodrigo Sorogoyen en la que interpreta, precisamente, a un padre ausente.
Y, claro, aunque estamos hablando de superestrellas que tratan de evitar no ver a sus hijos durante semanas, "uno de los dos debe estar siempre con ellos" suena a lo que suena: a helicópteros.
¿Helicópteros? ¿Perdona? En 1969, el psicólogo Haim Ginott publicó Between Parent & Teenager, un libro elaborado en base a conversaciones con adolescentes. En una de ellas, un chaval describía a su madre como un "helicóptero". Y la imagen ha hecho fortuna para definir un tipo de crianza que, básicamente, consiste en tener siempre a un padre detrás de los niños.
El problema es que era más una forma peyorativa de hablar de los padres modernos que algo que supiéramos definir.
Hasta 2024. Ese año, unos investigadores de Griffith y varias universidad europeas se hicieron una pregunta que daría muchos frutos: ¿"sobreproteger" es una sola conducta? Y la respuesta, claro, es que no.
Sé que va a parecer una obviedad, pero los análisis factoriales separaron dos tipos de 'estar presente': el primero es 'demandante' (controlar, restringir, decidir por el niño) y el otro es 'responsivo' (estar disponible).
Mientras el estilo demandante correlaciona negativamente con la autonomía del hijo y positivamente con la ansiedad (y el burnout) de los padres. El otro estilo hacía justo lo contrario. Y es curioso porque llevamos décadas juntado los dos estilo como si fuera uno solo.
Y entender eso nos está ayudando mucho. Hace un puñado de meses, Clinical Child and Family Psychology Review publicó un metaanálisis que trataba el efecto de la crianza intrusiva en los niños. Según sus datos (que cubren más de 150.000 participantes), la correlación entre estilos intrusivos y síntomas internalizantes como la ansiedad o la depresión es de 0,24.
Lo curioso aparece cuando desglosamos esos datos: el peor estilo es el control psicológico (invalidar, manipular emocionales, etc...), seguido de la sobre protección y la falta de apoyo a la autonomía. Por último el 'hilicopter parenting' propiamente dicho.
Es decir, no importa tanto "el estar" como "lo que se hace mientras se está".
Nunca fueron las horas. Esto ya estaba en la investigación previa. En 2015, Milkie, Nomaguchi y Denny midieron directamente la cantidad de tiempo que niños y adolescentes pasaban con sus padres. Sus conclusiones fueron que, en los pequeños, el tiempo materno no se asociaban con conductas o emociones problemáticas, ni con caídas en el rendimiento. En los adolescentes apareció una sola asociación entre la implicación materna y una menor conducta delictiva; pero, sinceramente, es muy pequeño.
En todo caso, los mejores efectos aparecían cuando ambos progenitores estaban con los niños a la vez (menos problemas de conducta, mejores notas en matemáticas, menos consumo de sustancias, etc...). Antes de eso, en 2000, Stattin y Kerr habían dejado claro que lo que protegía a un adolescente no era que el padre les vigilara, sino que el hijo contara las cosas por iniciativa propia. No es cuanto, es cómo.
¿Y por qué nos preocupa tanto el tiempo? Paradójicamente porque ahora estamos mucho más tiempo con los niños que antes. Según Giulia Dotti Sani y Judith Treas, entre 1965 y 2012, las madres pasaron de 54 a 104 minutos diarios de cuidado directo y los padres de 16 a 59.
Como decían Jose César Perales y Fátima García en una entrevista que aún no hemos publicado, quizás el mayor cambio de la crianza de los últimos años es que ahora nos importan genuínamente los niños. Mucho más que antes. Y eso hace que el malestar de la infancia cause dolor también en los adultos.
Sin mucho motivo. Tras revisar toda esta investigación solo hay algo seguro: que los efectos son diminutos y hay una enorme heterogeneidad entre estudios. Como defendió Sandra Scarr, por encima de un umbral de cuidado suficiente, las diferencias entre estilos de crianza dejan de predecir resultados. Lo importante, ahora como siempre, es hacerlo lo mejor que uno pueda.

articles.title: AKS Looks to Make Node Disruption More Predictable with New NAP Guidance
articles.text:
Microsoft is placing greater emphasis on controlling disruption in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) Node Auto-Provisioning (NAP), publishing new guidance to help platform teams balance the efficiency benefits of automated node consolidation with application availability. The central message is that NAP's ability to automatically remove, replace, and consolidate nodes needs to be governed at both the workload and infrastructure layers if Kubernetes environments are to remain predictable during scale-downs, upgrades, and maintenance.
NAP, which is based on the open-source Karpenter project, automatically provisions and manages nodes in response to pending workloads and can subsequently remove underutilized infrastructure. While this can improve bin-packing and reduce cloud costs, automated node removal introduces another form of change into the Kubernetes environment. Microsoft says many of the operational problems users encounter are related to how workloads respond when NAP attempts to drain and remove a node.
Microsoft's guidance emphasizes two complementary mechanisms. At the application layer, Kubernetes Pod Disruption Budgets (PDBs) determine how many replicas can be voluntarily evicted during operations such as node consolidation. At the infrastructure layer, NAP provides controls governing how and when nodes themselves can be disrupted. These include consolidation policies, disruption budgets, node expiration and drift management.
The distinction is important because these mechanisms solve different problems. A PDB protects an application's availability, while NAP's disruption controls regulate the pace and circumstances under which infrastructure is changed. Microsoft recommends using the two together rather than expecting either mechanism to provide complete protection on its own.
One of the most useful warnings in the guidance concerns overly restrictive Pod Disruption Budgets. A PDB configured with maxUnavailable: 0, or effectively requiring 100% of replicas to remain available, can prevent Kubernetes from voluntarily evicting pods indefinitely. That can leave NAP unable to drain nodes, meaning consolidation, upgrades, and migrations can become stuck.
The answer is not simply to loosen every PDB. Instead, teams need to align disruption policies with the actual availability requirements of each workload. For sufficiently replicated services, allowing a small amount of voluntary disruption, for example, one unavailable replica, can allow infrastructure maintenance to proceed without creating a meaningful customer impact.
NAP's consolidation capability illustrates the broader trade-off. When configured with WhenEmptyOrUnderutilized, NAP can evaluate whether workloads could be moved onto a more efficient combination of virtual machines and then remove unnecessary capacity. Operators can also delay consolidation using consolidateAfter, while expireAfter can enforce a maximum node lifetime.
This turns infrastructure optimization into a continuous decision-making process. The platform is effectively asking: Can I run these workloads more efficiently without violating the constraints placed around them? That is powerful, but it also means that Kubernetes operators need to understand the policies influencing those decisions rather than treating autoscaling as an opaque mechanism.
Microsoft also makes an important distinction between voluntary and involuntary disruption. NAP's disruption controls and Kubernetes PDBs primarily govern voluntary operations such as consolidation, drift, and node expiration. They do not prevent events such as hardware failures, host failures, or Azure Spot VM evictions
For Spot instances in particular, disruption is part of the economic model. AKS can detect an impending eviction and begin provisioning replacement capacity, but applications using Spot infrastructure still need to be designed to tolerate interruption.
This is increasingly relevant beyond AKS. Kubernetes itself is moving toward more sophisticated node provisioning and consolidation capabilities, while Karpenter provides similar concepts across cloud environments. The Kubernetes documentation describes node autoscaling as a mechanism for dynamically provisioning and consolidating nodes to respond to demand and optimize cost.
The challenge for platform engineering teams is therefore shifting from "How do we make Kubernetes scale?" to "How do we make automated scaling safe?". Microsoft's NAP guidance provides a useful model: protect workloads with application-level availability constraints, control infrastructure changes with disruption policies, and deliberately define which workloads can tolerate interruption.
As Kubernetes becomes increasingly autonomous, particularly as clusters support increasingly expensive AI and data workloads, the ability to control when infrastructure changes, how much can change at once, and what happens when something goes wrong may become just as important as the ability to provision capacity in the first place.

articles.title: Outlander : Blood of my Blood (HBO Max) – Un trailer brutal et intense pour la saison 2

Outlander : Blood of my Blood (HBO Max) – Un trailer brutal et intense pour la saison 2
La guerre s'installe dans les Highlands dans la bande-annonce de la deuxième saison de la série Outlander : Blood of my Blood, attendue sur le service de streaming HBO Max en septembre.
Guerre, romance déchirée et voyage dans le temps sont au programme de la saison 2 de la série préquelle d'Outlander. Programmés sur HBO Max en septembre, les nouveaux épisodes d'Outlander : Blood of my Blood se dévoilent dans une bande-annonce qui laisse entrevoir bien des obstacles à affronter pour les héros de cette série en kilt.
Tout le monde doit choisir son camp
Outlander : Blood of my Blood est un spin-off d'Outlander chroniquant l'histoire des parents de Jamie Fraser et Claire Beauchamp, les personnages au cœur de cette fiction historique adaptée des romans de Diana Gabaldon.
Créée par Matthew B. Roberts (Outlander), Blood of my Blood mélange l'Écosse du 18e siècle à la science-fiction avec des personnages capables de voyager dans le temps.
Dans la saison 2, la révolte jacobite de 1715 gronde et tout le monde à un combat à mener. Pendant que Brian Fraser (Jamie Roy) est occupé sur le champ de bataille, Ellen MacKenzie (Harriet Slater) doit faire face à la guerre qui fait rage au sein de sa propre famille.
Toujours dans les années 1700, Julia Beauchamp (Hermione Corfield) est une nouvelle fois séparée de son mari Henry (Jeremy Irvine), qui a lui réussi à retourner vers le futur. Mais si ces images indiquent bien une chose, c'est que ce retour au 20e siècle ne va pas être facile pour l'ancien soldat. Il va devoir faire face à ses troubles mentaux s'il espère retrouver Julia.
Le reste de la distribution est complété par Tony Curran dans le rôle de Simon Fraser, Séamus McLean Ross sous les traits de Colum MacKenzie, Sam Retford dans les bottes de Dougal MacKenzie, Rory Alexander dans le rôle de Murtagh Fitzgibbons Fraser et Conor MacNeill dans celui de Ned Gowan.
Outlander : Blood of my Blood sera de retour en streaming sur HBO Max à partir du 19 septembre prochain.

articles.title: Smartphone « écologique » : l’Europe veut mettre un terme au « greenwashing » des entreprises tech
articles.text:
Que ce soit en magasin ou sur des sites de e-commerce, vous avez sans doute déjà été confronté à des produits tech présentés comme « écologiques » ou étiquetés « zéro émission de carbone ». À l’heure où la question de l’écologie occupe une place centrale dans le débat public, ces arguments peuvent retenir l’attention, d’autant plus lorsque l’on connaît l’impact de la tech sur l’environnement. Mais certaines entreprises trompent les consommateurs en pratiquant du greenwashing. Justement, l’Union européenne entend y mettre un terme grâce à une nouvelle directive.
L’Europe s’attaque au greenwashing dans la tech
Le 27 septembre prochain, l’Union européenne va mettre en œuvre la directive (UE) 202/825. Son objectif : mettre un terme au greenwashing pratiqué par certaines entreprises de la tech. Un exemple ? Apple a présenté pendant un certain temps les Apple Watch et le Mac mini comme « neutres en carbone ». Inutile de préciser que cela n’est pas le cas dans les faits.
L’Europe veut ainsi bannir les « allégations environnementales trompeuses » qui « se fonderaient sur la compensation des émissions de gaz à effet de serre pour affirmer qu’un produit a une incidence neutre, réduite ou positive sur l’environnement ». Pour l’UE, ce type de promesses « donne l’impression erronée que la consommation de ce produit n’a pas d’incidence sur l’environnement ». Les exemples de slogans publicitaires sous couvert d’écologie sont multiples : « écologique », « respectueux de la planète », « neutre en carbone », « respectueux de l’environnement », « neutre pour le climat » ou encore « climatiquement compensé ».
De la même façon, les descriptions floues seront dans le viseur de l’Union européenne. Un produit ne peut ainsi pas être présenté comme soucieux de l’environnement seulement parce que son emballage contient des matériaux recyclés. Aussi, les promesses de conditions de travail dignes seront étudiées de près par l’UE.
Quelles conséquences pour les entreprises tech qui proposent leurs produits en Europe ?
En réalité, ces labels, promesses et arguments publicitaires ne seront pas interdits en Europe. Les entreprises pourront toujours les utiliser, à condition toutefois de pouvoir prouver qu’ils correspondent à la réalité. Une entreprise annonce que son nouveau téléphone est écologique et qu’il a été conçu dans le respect des conditions de travail ? Elle devra être en mesure de le prouver. Pour les fabricants, cela implique donc de pouvoir documenter davantage leurs affirmations environnementales et sociales avant de les mettre en avant dans leurs campagnes publicitaires. Autant dire que cela s’annonce plus compliqué que d’imaginer des slogans et labels verts dans une salle de réunion. L’Union européenne nous a quant à elle démontré ces derniers temps qu’elle n’hésitait pas à infliger des amendes salées aux entreprises qui ne respectent pas ses règles.

articles.title: Por qué un aire acondicionado sucio puede disparar el cobro del recibo de luz
articles.text:
Durante los meses de mayor calor, muchas personas experimentan un aumento en la factura de electricidad debido al uso frecuente del aire acondicionado. Un factor, aunque a menudo ignorado, es el estado de limpieza del aparato. El electrodoméstico sucio no solo afecta la calidad del ambiente interior, sino que puede disparar de manera considerable el consumo eléctrico, incrementando los gastos del hogar sin que el usuario lo note de inmediato.
Cómo influye la suciedad en el consumo de energía del aire acondicionado
La acumulación de polvo y grasa en los componentes internos del aire acondicionado genera una serie de obstáculos en el funcionamiento del sistema. Esta suciedad obstruye el flujo de aire, dificultando la transferencia de calor y obligando al aparato a operar a máxima potencia durante más tiempo para alcanzar la temperatura programada.
PUBLICIDAD
Como resultado, la unidad consume mucha más electricidad de la necesaria, lo que repercute directamente en un aumento del monto a pagar en el recibo de luz.
El principal motivo de este exceso de consumo radica en que el sistema debe trabajar de manera constante y forzada. La falta de mantenimiento provoca que elementos como los filtros, el evaporador y el condensador acumulen suciedad, lo que impacta negativamente en el rendimiento general del equipo.
PUBLICIDAD
Según CYE Energía, “un equipo sucio trabaja forzado y consume mucha más electricidad. Es fundamental limpiar los filtros periódicamente y realizar un mantenimiento adecuado para asegurar su eficiencia energética”.
El compresor, que es el componente que más energía demanda, se ve especialmente afectado por la falta de limpieza. Cuando el aparato no logra enfriar la estancia de manera eficiente, el compresor se mantiene en funcionamiento continuo, incrementando el consumo de kilovatios-hora (kWh). Incluso modelos más modernos, como los que cuentan con tecnología Inverter, sufren este problema si el mantenimiento no es el adecuado.
PUBLICIDAD
Factores que incrementan el consumo eléctrico en equipos sucios
Existen varias causas concretas que explican por qué un aire acondicionado sucio requiere más energía para funcionar. La primera, según Gemini, es la obstrucción de los filtros de aire. Cuando estos están saturados de polvo, el ventilador tiene que esforzarse más para aspirar el aire del entorno. Esta reducción en el flujo de aire provoca que el aparato tarde más tiempo en enfriar el espacio, lo que mantiene el motor encendido de manera constante.
Otra causa frecuente es el aislamiento térmico provocado por el polvo en el evaporador. Cuando las serpentinas interiores se cubren de suciedad, el refrigerante no puede absorber correctamente el calor del aire. Esto reduce el rendimiento del sistema y obliga a que funcione a menor capacidad de lo que fue diseñado.
PUBLICIDAD
La suciedad también afecta al condensador exterior, que puede llenarse de tierra y residuos. Si el serpentín exterior no libera el calor acumulado debido a la suciedad, la presión interna del sistema aumenta, lo que se traduce en un mayor esfuerzo eléctrico por parte del compresor para mantener el funcionamiento.
Un problema adicional que señala la IA de Google es el congelamiento de las tuberías, causado por la falta de flujo de aire sobre un evaporador sucio. La humedad atrapada se congela y forma una capa de hielo, bloqueando completamente el paso del aire. En este escenario, el aparato sigue trabajando sin poder enfriar el ambiente, generando un consumo continuo y sin resultados efectivos.
PUBLICIDAD
Consejos para reducir el consumo de energía del aire acondicionado
Optimizar el uso del aire acondicionado es clave para evitar sorpresas en la factura. Uno de los consejos más efectivos es ajustar el termostato a una temperatura moderada, entre 25 y 26 grados, siguiendo las recomendaciones del Instituto para la Diversificación del Ahorro y la Energía (IDAE).
Cada grado adicional que se baja en el termostato puede aumentar el gasto energético entre un 5 % y un 7 %. Por ello, mantener una temperatura estable y no excesivamente baja ayuda no solo a ahorrar, sino también a reducir el impacto ambiental.
PUBLICIDAD
También es relevante elegir el modo de funcionamiento adecuado. Los equipos modernos incluyen un modo “eco” o “ahorro de energía” que regula automáticamente la temperatura para minimizar el consumo eléctrico, manteniendo a la vez el confort en el hogar. Usar la velocidad del ventilador en modo bajo y permitir el movimiento alternado de las aspas contribuye a distribuir el aire de manera uniforme y eficiente.
El uso de termostatos programables o temporizadores facilita el encendido y apagado del aparato según las necesidades del hogar. Apagar el aire acondicionado cuando la casa está vacía o durante la noche, cuando la temperatura exterior es más baja, permite evitar un consumo innecesario.
PUBLICIDAD
Horas de mayor consumo de aire acondicionado y recomendaciones para un uso eficiente
El aire acondicionado requiere más energía durante las horas centrales del día, especialmente entre las 12 y las 16 horas, cuando las temperaturas exteriores alcanzan su punto más alto. Es en este intervalo cuando el equipo necesita trabajar con mayor intensidad para mantener el ambiente fresco, incrementando así el gasto eléctrico.
Además, intentar enfriar los espacios a temperaturas muy bajas aumenta la diferencia térmica entre el interior y el exterior, lo que fuerza al sistema a operar de manera más exigente y prolongada.
PUBLICIDAD
En cuanto a la pregunta sobre si es mejor dejar el aparato encendido o apagarlo cuando se sale de la habitación, la respuesta depende del tiempo de ausencia. Los sistemas de aire acondicionado consumen más durante el arranque, pero mantenerlos encendidos todo el día sin necesidad es menos eficiente y genera un gasto innecesario. Utilizar temporizadores o programadores permite encontrar un equilibrio entre comodidad y ahorro.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: X says China used hundreds of bot accounts to amplify fears about AI data centers that many Americans already share
articles.text:
A hot potato: X says that it has just identified a bot farm of approximately 200,000 accounts created by Chinese operators. What's getting a lot of attention is that 200 of these accounts were apparently dedicated to posting anti-AI data center content designed to influence public perception. The country has tried this before with little success – most people already hate the facilities, anyway.
X's Global Government Affairs writes that the 200 accounts were posting "in a manner that could manipulate a legitimate debate about American AI and energy policy."
The posts contained "claims" that AI data centers are driving up household electricity prices and straining the grid. Other posts featured AI-generated cartoons that depicted data-center operators enriching themselves at the public's expense.
 – Global Government Affairs (@GlobalAffairs) August 28, 2026
At least two of the example images appeared in a similar OpenAI report from June. It claimed that China-based ChatGPT users asked the chatbot for ways to influence Americans' opinions of data centers in the US. The resulting posts also claimed that AI data center buildouts for AI were increasing electricity prices for average families.
When discussing rising electricity prices, the OpenAI report said the accounts "claimed" this was the case. But it really is happening, as noted by Bloomberg, which found that prices have risen by up to 267% in areas near data centers.
Goldman Sachs came to a similar conclusion. It wrote that electricity prices have already increased by 6.9% year-over-year as of February 2026, and they'll continue to increase as more AI data centers are built.
X didn't say what the remaining 198,800 accounts were posting. OpenAI's June report said the other main content criticized US tariffs and technology policies, so one could assume the same thing was happening here.
The pushback against data centers in the US has been growing in both size and intensity. It's led to claims that the opposition hurts the economy and national security. Fox News compared it to protesting against tank and plane factories during World War II. Even President Donald Trump said those opposing the construction of new data centers are "making a mistake."
Ultimately, it feels like China is wasting its time trying to convince people of something they already believe. The facilities consume enormous amounts of electricity and can strain power grids that were never designed for such concentrated demand. One planned Michigan campus is expected to draw 1.4 gigawatts – roughly the output of a nuclear power plant – while residents have also raised concerns about traffic and the loss of agricultural land.
Water use is another major concern. Virginia data centers consumed at least 1.85 billion gallons in 2023, up from 1.13 billion gallons in 2019. In Georgia, one development used 29 million gallons of water before receiving a bill while nearby residents complained about low water pressure.
The expansion can also bring constant noise and more pollution, especially as operators turn to diesel generators and gas turbines when the grid cannot keep up. China may be exploiting the controversy, but it certainly didn't invent it.

articles.title: Meta makes AI glasses slightly less creepy with limit on nonconsensual recording
articles.text:
Meta is rolling out an obvious fix to make its AI glasses less creepy amid backlash over the glasses’ non-consensual recordings that have flooded the Internet.
On Friday, The Verge reported that Meta closed a loophole that made it easy for smart glasses users to cover up an LED light that is supposed to alert bystanders that the device is actively recording. Meta had previously deactivated recording if a user attempted to start capturing video after placing a sticker over the light, but people quickly learned that they could get around that by reversing the order of the steps and covering up the light after they started recording.
In a post on Threads, Meta’s executive vice president of wearables, Alex Himel, explained that an update would be rolled out soon that ensures that “the camera will now stop working if the light is covered during a recording.” That way “the capture LED can reliably alert bystanders when photos or videos are being captured for someone’s gallery,” Himel said.
According to Himel, “only a tiny minority of people try to get around these protections, and the fact they have to go to these lengths shows our efforts are working. We’ll keep improving and evolving our approach.”
However, bad actors may still be able to modify the glasses or tamper with the light without affecting recordings. And it’s unclear if popular bypasses, like using semi-transparent stickers that make the light less noticeable, would block recording under Meta’s new safeguard.
Data regulators in the European Union are currently probing privacy concerns with Meta’s glasses and have suggested that Meta may not have properly field-tested the LED light to ensure that the public would understand its safety functionality. Germany is considering banning the glasses after a nonprofit filed a criminal complaint alleging that they breach Germany’s strict privacy laws, Politico reported. And Germany is not alone, as many countries in the EU mull a crackdown on the technology, which they see as invasive and carrying a risk of expanding mass surveillance. Another Politico report confirmed that the European Data Protection Board will release a report later this summer to decide what actions should be taken to ensure no one in the EU is recorded without their consent.

articles.title: PowerColor Launches AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT Hellhound Resonance Edition
articles.text:
Friday, August 28th 2026
	
		
	
	
	
PowerColor Launches AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT Hellhound Resonance Edition
PowerColor, in collaboration with AMD and Focus Entertainment, today announced the PowerColor Hellhound AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT 16 GB GDDR6 Resonance Edition, a special edition graphics card that brings the world of Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy to life. Blending striking, game-inspired aesthetics with the exceptional performance of AMD RDNA 4 architecture, the Resonance Edition is an immersive companion for every step of the journey, and every Resonance Edition includes a full game code and an exclusive themed mousepad, so the hardware built for the adventure and the adventure itself arrive in one box.
A World Worth Fighting For
Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy is the next chapter in Focus Entertainment's acclaimed A Plague Tale saga, a series celebrated by players and critics alike for its unforgettable storytelling and breathtaking world. Following Sophia on a journey where survival is the only path forward and mysterious secrets lie hidden beneath the island's depths; the game has captured the imagination of a passionate community of story-driven gamers. With the Resonance Edition, PowerColor invites that community to carry the adventure from the screen into the heart of their build.The Legacy Takes Physical Form
The Hellhound's signature backplate is reimagined with exclusive artwork from Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy, Sophia and the world of the game rendered across the card in rich, weathered golds, turning every build into a piece of the story. Completing the look, the Hellhound's lighting is transformed into an amber glow with a dual-stage switch, evoking the warmth of a fading sunset drawn directly from the world of the game.
Hellhound Engineering, Proven in Battle
Beneath the artwork lives everything that has made the Hellhound a favorite of reviewers and builders alike. Powered by AMD RDNA 4 architecture with 64 compute units and 16 GB of GDDR6 memory running at 20.0 Gbps on a 256-bit bus, the Resonance Edition reaches a Boost Clock of up to 3010 MHz in OC mode, with Dual BIOS offering a near-silent alternative profile on demand.
Hellhound RX 9070 XT Architecture and Performance
A 2.5-slot triple ring-fan cooler with reverse-rotation fans and premium Japanese dual ball bearings keeps thermals firmly in check, aided by Honeywell PTM7950 phase-change thermal interface material and a large GPU direct-contact copper plate spanning the GPU and VRAM. A 10+1 phase power design on a 12-layer high-conductivity PCB delivers rock-solid stability, while the Intelligent Fan Controller keeps the card fully passive below 50°C for whisper-quiet idle and light gaming.
The Journey Comes With You
Every Resonance Edition includes a full game code for Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy - day one, you're playing. Also in the box: the PowerColor Gaming Mousepad Resonance Edition, designed for precision and comfort and featuring artwork inspired by the game, bringing the world of Resonance to the entire setup. Game codes are redeemable until August 26th, 2027.
Availability
The PowerColor Hellhound AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT GPU Resonance Edition will be available beginning August 28, 2026, through selected PowerColor partners and retailers in participating markets.

articles.title: Nvidia denies pausing AI cloud commitments initiative after reported partner backlash — report claims company told cloud providers it could only lease its GPUs to Nvidia-approved customers
articles.text:
Nvidia denies pausing AI cloud commitments initiative after reported partner backlash — report claims company told cloud providers it could only lease its GPUs to Nvidia-approved customers
Why pause after giving $36 billion of commitments?
Nvidia on Friday denied a report by the Wall Street Journal claiming that the company had put some transactions under its recently introduced 'take or pay' AI Compute Partnership on hold, less than two months after unveiling the initiative in early July and days before detailing the effort in its earnings call. The transactions were reportedly paused as some partners were irritated with Nvidia's attempts to influence their operations and because it raised internal concerns about potential antitrust scrutiny.
"The new business model we introduced in July that opens up compute access to the fast-growing AI ecosystem is still in place and continues to evolve due to high demand," a spokesperson for Nvidia told Tom's Hardware.
The report itself does not establish that Nvidia has abandoned the AI Compute Partnership program under which the company committed to rent capacity of newly built AI data centers as well as their minimum revenue, but claims that it put some deals on hold. Meanwhile, Nvidia's denial indicates that the program continues to exist, but is evolving, which means changing.
Per the report, it looks like Nvidia attempted to control how its 'AI Compute Partners' rented their capacity. The company told some cloud providers participating in the program that they could lease its GPUs only to customers approved by Nvidia, according to the WSJ report. The company also preferred to spread available capacity across multiple smaller AI companies instead of allowing a single large customer to take most or all of it. Some cloud operators reportedly pushed back against these restrictions, arguing that they should retain control over which customers they serve. Perhaps, in turn, Nvidia put some of the deals on hold.
While Nvidia does not lend any money or directly finance AI data center buildouts (which essentially means circular financing), it provides demand commitments and guaranteed revenue levels, which perhaps raised internal concerns about potential antitrust scrutiny. As a result, Nvidia could be revising the terms of the deals it inks with partners.
$36 billion of commitments
Modern AI data centers cost billions of dollars that must be spent on the premises, infrastructure, and compute hardware well before an operator has secured enough customer contracts to finance the buildout. Meanwhile, banks or infrastructure investors want confidence that enough of the future facility capacity will actually be rented. Under the program, Nvidia intends to use its own demand commitment on a portion of the facility's capacity in exchange for a percentage of the facility's revenue if demand is strong. This makes financing AI data centers easier as from the lender's perspective, part of the project's revenue stream is effectively supported by Nvidia rather than depending entirely on the operator's ability to find customers.
"Nvidia provides a take-or-pay commitment on a portion of the facility's capacity, a minimum revenue guarantee that gives lenders the confidence to underwrite the project, and in exchange, we share in a portion of the NeoCloud's revenue earned above that floor," explained Colette Kress, chief financial officer of Nvidia, during the company's earnings call. "In this model, we get paid twice, once on the hardware sale, and again through the share of rental revenue, a highly recurring stream layered on top of a one-time equipment purchase."
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
While actual percentages and economic terms have not been disclosed, it should work pretty straightforwardly. Nvidia provides a take-or-pay commitment that it rents, say, 30% of the capacity of a newly built facility and a minimum revenue guarantee over a period of six years. If the demand is strong and the facility rents 80% of its capacity, well exceeding the minimum revenue guarantee, Nvidia does not need to absorb the guaranteed capacity, and because revenue exceeds the agreed floor, Nvidia receives a percentage of the excess revenue. If the demand is weak and the facility can only rent 20% of its capacity, running well below the guaranteed revenue level, Nvidia's take-or-pay obligation would require it to cover the difference between actual revenue and the contracted minimum according to the specific agreement. Alternatively, Nvidia could rent back unused compute capacity for its own needs and cover the difference between the actual and guaranteed revenue level.
While at least some participants were reportedly irritated with Nvidia's alleged control of tenants, the program has proven to be quite a success so far. As of late July, just weeks after formally announcing the program, Nvidia had committed $36 billion in these new agreements that run for six years.
"Our commitments, which are typically six years in duration, totaled $36 billion as of July 26, 2026," an Nvidia filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission reads.
Nvidia has not disclosed which portions of monetizable capacities it typically commits, so it is impossible to figure out the value of the hardware it intends to supply under the $36 billion commitments.
