articles.title: The forgotten bestseller that predicted quiet quitting
articles.text:
The forgotten bestseller that predicted quiet quitting
Discover why a forgotten workplace bestseller feels surprisingly relevant in the age of quiet quitting, burnout, and shifting career values.
The rise of quiet quitting has sparked conversations about work-life balance, employee engagement, burnout, and the changing relationship between workers and employers.
While the term itself is relatively new, the concerns behind it are not. Decades ago, writers and thinkers were already questioning workplace culture, conformity, and the expectation that employees should devote themselves entirely to their organisations.
One forgotten bestseller that feels remarkably relevant today is The Organisation Man by William H. Whyte. First published in 1956, the book examined how corporate culture shaped individual identity and questioned whether unquestioning loyalty to organisations came at the expense of personal fulfilment.
Although written in a very different era, many of its observations echo concerns that continue to shape modern workplaces.
This forgotten book predicted quiet quitting years ago
In The Organisation Man, William H. Whyte explored the rise of large corporations and the growing expectation that employees should place the needs of the organisation above their own ambitions, values, and individuality.
He observed a culture where conformity was often rewarded and where success was closely tied to fitting into a corporate system. Whyte questioned whether this model truly benefited workers and warned that excessive organisational loyalty could sometimes limit personal freedom and independent thinking.
While the workplace has changed dramatically since the 1950s, the book's central question remains relevant: how much of ourselves should we give to our jobs?
Today, many workers are reassessing expectations around constant availability, unpaid overtime, and the idea that professional success should define personal worth. In many ways, quiet quitting reflects a similar desire to establish healthier boundaries between work and life.
Why the book feels relevant today
One reason The Organisation Man resonates with modern readers is its focus on workplace identity. Many employees today are questioning whether career achievement should remain the primary measure of success.
Quiet quitting is often less about doing the minimum and more about rejecting the expectation that work should consume every aspect of life.
Whyte's observations about organisational pressure and social expectations feel strikingly familiar in an era where burnout has become a common concern.
The book also highlights how workplace cultures can influence behaviour. Employees frequently adapt their values, priorities, and even personalities to align with organisational expectations.
Modern discussions about workplace wellness, flexible schedules, and work-life balance suggest that many people are actively seeking alternatives to these pressures.
The connection between quiet quitting and workplace culture
Quiet quitting has often been misunderstood as a lack of ambition. For many workers, however, it represents a decision to perform their responsibilities without allowing work to dominate their personal lives. This shift reflects broader questions about what people expect from their careers.
Whyte's book anticipated these debates by examining the tension between individual goals and organisational demands. He recognised that people often struggle to balance personal fulfilment with professional expectations.
His work suggests that when organisations expect excessive loyalty without providing meaningful rewards, employees naturally begin to reassess the relationship.
What can modern readers learn from it?
Although The Organisation Man was written nearly seventy years ago, its insights remain surprisingly useful. The book encourages readers to think critically about workplace norms rather than accepting them automatically.
It asks important questions about ambition, success, independence, and personal values. Modern readers may find that the book offers historical context for conversations happening today.
It shows that concerns about workplace pressure, conformity, and employee well-being did not suddenly appear with quiet quitting. Instead, they have been developing for generations.
The lasting message
The enduring value of The Organisation Man lies in its reminder that work is only one part of a meaningful life. Careers can provide purpose, stability, and achievement, but they should not require the complete sacrifice of personal identity.
As discussions about quiet quitting, burnout, and work-life balance continue, this forgotten bestseller offers a thoughtful perspective on questions that many people are still trying to answer. Its message encourages a healthier and more balanced relationship with work, one that recognises both professional responsibilities and personal well-being.

articles.title: China desafía a Samsung y SK hynix: YMTC aspira a dominar el mercado mundial de chips NAND en 2027
articles.text:
La crisis que ha desencadenado el apetito voraz de los centros de datos por las memorias y los microprocesadores representa una gran oportunidad para los fabricantes chinos de chips DRAM y NAND. Las compañías surcoreanas SK hynix y Samsung Electronics, y la estadounidense Micron Technology, lideran este mercado, pero para dar respuesta a la demanda han reasignado alrededor del 70% de sus líneas de producción a las memorias de alto ancho de banda (HBM por su denominación en inglés).
Las consecuencias de este movimiento no tardaron en aparecer: las memorias DDR4 y DDR5 estándar y sus derivados, que son las más utilizadas en el segmento de consumo, empezaron inmediatamente a escasear. Y su precio se disparó. El fabricante chino de chips DRAM CXMT (Changxin Memory Technologies) está intentando aprovechar esta coyuntura para capturar la parte del mercado que en gran medida han abandonado Samsung, SK hynix y Micron, pero en China hay otro actor importante en este escenario: YMTC (Yangtze Memory Technologies Co.).
Esta compañía es uno de los mayores fabricantes de chips NAND. Su cuota en el mercado global es aproximadamente del 14%, por lo que es uno de los principales competidores de Samsung, SK hynix, Micron, Kioxia o SanDisk. Su peso en el mercado chino es muy grande, sobre todo debido a que las sanciones de EEUU impiden a sus competidores estadounidenses y surcoreanos vender a sus clientes chinos sus circuitos integrados más sofisticados. Pero YMTC está decidida a crecer más. Mucho más. Y tiene un plan.
Objetivo: liderar el mercado NAND en 2027
El diario económico Financial Times ha confirmado que los máximos responsables de YMTC han anticipado a los inversores de la compañía en las reuniones previas a su salida a bolsa que pretenden erigirse como el mayor fabricante de chips NAND antes de que acabe 2027. Es una ambición legítima, pero llevarla a buen puerto plantea un desafío enorme debido a que YMTC va a tener que casi duplicar su cuota de mercado durante los próximos 16 meses. Y el liderazgo actual de Samsung y SK hynix es robusto.
El plan de la cúpula directiva de esta compañía china pasa por aprovechar su salida a bolsa para capturar 4.900 millones de dólares
Según Counterpoint Research, durante el segundo trimestre de 2026 Samsung ha sostenido una cuota en el mercado NAND del 25%; SK hynix, junto con su filial Solidigm, del 22%; e YMTC ocupa la tercera posición con un 14% de cuota mundial. Para superar a Samsung, como he mencionado unas líneas más arriba, casi va a tener que duplicar su cuota de mercado. El plan de la cúpula directiva de esta compañía china pasa por aprovechar su salida a bolsa para capturar 4.900 millones de dólares en el mercado STAR de Shanghái.
Una parte de ese dinero estará destinada a la mejora de las líneas de fabricación. Y otra, a investigación avanzada. En cualquier caso, YMTC no tiene a su favor solo la crisis que está asolando el mercado de los chips DRAM y NAND; su itinerario durante los últimos dos años ha sido sorprendente. En 2023 no era una compañía rentable, pero su margen bruto ha pasado del 5,45% de 2023 a nada menos que el 76,77% durante el primer trimestre de 2026. Sus fábricas actualmente están al 98% de su capacidad de producción.
CXMT capturó 8.600 millones de dólares en julio y llegó a superar el valor bursátil de Tencent, lo que refleja que el apetito de los inversores por las compañías chinas de circuitos integrados es voraz. De hecho, YMTC va a utilizar su salida a bolsa como un mecanismo de financiación conectado íntimamente con la estrategia del Gobierno chino que persigue alcanzar la autosuficiencia tecnológica. Los altos márgenes de las empresas chinas de chips están financiando el desarrollo de herramientas de producción nacionales. Y, por otro lado, el mercado de Shanghái les permite acceder al capital que necesitan más allá de la presión que ejerce EEUU.

articles.title: Samsung ouvre Quick Share aux iPhone : la liste des smartphones Galaxy compatibles
articles.text:
Samsung a officiellement lancé une fonction baptisée « Share with iOS devices » (partage avec les appareils iOS) via Quick Share. Concrètement, elle permet d’envoyer et de recevoir des fichiers (photos, vidéos, documents, etc.) entre un smartphone Galaxy et un iPhone de manière native, un peu comme AirDrop, mais en mode interécosystèmes.
Depuis quand et sur quelles versions de One UI ?
Afin d’en profiter, voici les quelques prérequis que votre smartphone Galaxy doit remplir :
- Versions de One UI requises : One UI 8.5 ou One UI 9 (basées sur Android 17 et Android 18) ;
- Application Quick Share version 13.8.51.27 ou supérieure ;
- Google Play Services version 26.11.xx ou supérieure.
Annoncée avec les Galaxy Z Fold 8 et Z Flip 8, la fonction est d’abord déployée sur ses flagships, à savoir les derniers pliants et les Galaxy S26, y compris le petit dernier, le Galaxy S26 FE. Une extension est ensuite prévue à d’autres modèles compatibles One UI 8.5/9 dans les mois suivants.
La liste des smartphones compatibles Quick Share vers iOS
En nous basant sur la base de données Android Update Tracker, nous pouvons donc arriver à une liste théorique des smartphones qui seront, à terme, compatibles. Comme vous pouvez le voir, la flotte est assez impressionnante, Samsung est loin de se limiter à quelques flagships flambant neufs.
Voici donc ci‑dessous, la liste complète des smartphones Samsung potentiellement compatibles avec Quick Share vers iOS une fois la fonction déployée sur leur modèle :

En pratique : comment vérifier si votre Galaxy est prêt
Pour maximiser vos chances d’avoir Quick Share vers iOS :

  -  Paramètres → À propos du téléphone → Informations sur le logiciel.
  -  Vous devez être sous One UI 8.5 ou One UI 9 (Android 17).
-  
-  Mettez à jour Quick Share et Google Play Services 
  -  Play Store → Recherche « Quick Share » → Mettez à jour si disponible.
  -  Play Store → Recherche « Google Play Services » → Mettez à jour.

articles.title: Malas noticias: este superventas de Motorola no se actualizará a Android 17
articles.text:
Hace tres años que Motorola lanzó un móvil de gama media con acabados premium y un precio rompedor. Tras su debut, el Motorola Edge 40 se convirtió en uno de los modelos más vendidos de la marca en Europa y América Latina. Lamentablemente para aquellos que lo compraron, este móvil no recibirá la esperada actualización a Android 17.
A diferencia de la familia Edge 50, el Motorola Edge 40 solo cuenta con dos años de actualizaciones de Android y tres años de parches de seguridad. La versión original se lanzó con Android 13, por lo que solo consiguió actualizarse hasta Android 15 antes de perder el soporte. Lo mismo ocurrió con la variante Edge 40 Neo, pero Motorola hizo una excepción con el Edge 40 Pro cuando decidió incluirlo en la lista de Android 16.
La decisión de no ofrecer la próxima versión de Android para el Motorola Edge 40 no debería sorprendernos, sobre todo si consideramos que se quedó con las ganas de Android 16. Las políticas de actualización de Motorola priorizan a los dispositivos de tope de gama, por lo que el Edge 40 Pro consiguió un último salto antes de quedar obsoleto. Independientemente de que se haya vendido por montones, al Edge 40 solo le queda conformarse con su más reciente actualización de seguridad.
El Motorola Edge 40 sigue siendo atractivo en 2026
Aunque se quede sin Android 17, el Edge 40 sigue siendo un móvil con buenas prestaciones para su rango de precio. Por menos de 250 euros obtienes una pantalla pOLED curva de 6,55 pulgadas con tasa de refresco de 144 Hz y 1.200 nits de brillo máximo. Por dentro incluye un procesador MediaTek Dimensity 8020, 8 GB de RAM y hasta 256 GB de almacenamiento.
En la parte fotográfica encontramos un sensor principal Sony Lytia de 50 MP con OIS, acompañado de un gran angular de 13 MP con función macro. La cámara frontal ofrece 32 MP para las selfies, la cual también está dotada de estabilización óptica de imagen y graba videos en 4K.
Al igual que sus hermanos mayores, el Motorola Edge 40 tiene un acabado premium con tonalidades Pantone y protección IP68. La oferta se completa con una batería de 4.400 mAh con carga rápida de 68 W por cable y 15 W de forma inalámbrica.
¿Qué hay de nuevo en Android 17 para los Motorola?
Si tienes un Motorola Edge 50 o cualquiera de los otros móviles compatibles, la actualización de Android 17 llegará con varias novedades. Una de las más notables tiene que ver con las notificaciones, ya que esta versión debuta las actualizaciones en vivo, una función con la que las aplicaciones muestran información en tiempo real. Los usuarios también podrán usar los resúmenes de notificaciones, que sintetizan el contenido de una conversación de WhatsApp o Mensajes para que no pierdas tiempo leyendo el chat completo.
Si tienes un Motorola de gama alta con buena pantalla, podrás aprovechar el nuevo control en el contenido HDR. Esta función te permitirá ajustar la intensidad del brillo en vídeos de YouTube o imágenes de Instagram y Google Fotos, de modo que tus ojos ya no sufrirán por las imágenes "quemadas" por el exceso de brillo en la configuración por defecto.
Otras funciones incluyen la posibilidad de ocultar las etiquetas de texto en el panel de ajustes rápidos, dos nuevas formas de compartir archivos con dispositivos conectados y mejoras en la seguridad. Motorola ya confirmó los primeros móviles compatibles con Android 17, aunque no reveló cuándo se lanzará la actualización. Conociendo lo lento que es el fabricante, es probable que tengamos que esperar varios meses para que esto se materialice.

articles.title: How to accelerate AI adoption without creating unnecessary security risk
articles.text:
How to accelerate AI adoption without creating unnecessary security risk
Balancing AI innovation with enterprise security governance
In the past eighteen months, our teams have moved from debating whether to use AI to debating how fast we can deploy it. The harder question is how to let teams move quickly enough to capture the value of AI without allowing the company’s risk profile to expand faster than its ability to govern it.
CTO and CISO at Entrata.
That tension is familiar to technology and security leaders because AI creates two mandates that can appear to compete with each other. The technology side of the organization wants experimentation, access, speed, and a path to real productivity gains, while the security side needs control, accountability, data boundaries, and confidence that new workflows will not introduce avoidable exposure.
Both instincts are correct, which is why companies get into trouble when they treat AI as either a pure innovation project or a pure security problem. It is an operating model change, and the organizations that handle it well will be the ones that build just enough structure and hardened tools to let teams move with confidence rather than forcing them to choose between speed and control.
Start with the work, not the tool
Many companies begin by treating AI adoption like a standard software rollout. They approve a vendor, distribute licenses, publish a few guidelines, and assume usage will naturally become transformative. That approach can create activity, but it rarely creates durable operational change.
Real adoption starts when leaders understand how work actually gets done. A finance team, product team, marketing team, support team, and engineering team will not use AI tools in the same way because each group has different knowledge requirements, data sources, risk thresholds, and experience. Each of these will require the development of AI skills and tools.
Leaders should begin by asking what each function is trying to accomplish, what knowledge it needs to make better decisions, what skills are required to use AI responsibly, and what tools or data sources are necessary to produce a reliable result.
When AI is mapped to those capabilities, it becomes part of how the organization operates; when it is layered on top of disconnected processes, it tends to create more output without necessarily creating better outcomes.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Treat data access as a risk design problem
Data access is one of the clearest places where AI changes the operating model. To make AI genuinely useful, teams often need access to information they did not previously use directly.
A marketing team may need product documentation and customer insights, a finance team may need structured operational data, and a support team may need internal knowledge, historical context, and the ability to understand patterns across systems.
The instinct to open access is understandable because AI becomes more valuable when it has more context. The instinct to restrict access is also understandable because broader access can create privacy, compliance, and security concerns. The answer is not to choose one instinct over the other but to create a more deliberate model for deciding which data can be used, by whom, and for what purpose.
In one enterprise rollout, for example, the practical answer was not to give every team access to everything or to keep AI locked inside a technical function. It was to separate lower-risk operational data from more sensitive information, then give teams enough access to work differently while limiting the potential damage if a workflow behaved unexpectedly.
One useful way to think about this is the blast radius of data. Not every dataset carries the same level of risk, and not every AI use case deserves the same level of restriction. Some information can be made more accessible because the potential damage is limited if something goes wrong, while other information, especially personally identifiable information or sensitive customer data, requires much tighter controls.
This approach allows teams to experiment where the risk is lower while preserving stronger governance where the business truly needs it. The goal is not to make security lighter, but to make it more precise so the company can move faster without losing control of the environments, data, and workflows that matter most.
Build verification into the workflow
Verification is where many AI strategies either become scalable or begin to stall. AI systems can produce work that looks polished but is incomplete, inaccurate, off-brand, or noncompliant, and while human review can absorb some of that risk in the early stages, it does not scale well once AI becomes embedded in daily operations.
I have seen this most clearly in technical teams, where AI can accelerate software development only if there is a reliable way to evaluate the quality, security, and accuracy of what gets produced. Without that verification layer, teams may feel faster in the moment while quietly creating more review burden, more rework, and more risk downstream.
Companies need verification patterns that are designed into the workflow itself. That can include automated checks, data quality controls, approval paths, logging, observability, and clear escalation rules for outputs that should not be trusted without further review.
Leaders shouldn't treat these mechanisms as bureaucracy added after the fact. They are what allow AI to move from individual productivity aid to enterprise capability, because teams can only scale adoption when they have a repeatable way to understand whether the work being produced is accurate, appropriate, and safe to use.
Make AI adoption a leadership responsibility
AI adoption cannot be delegated to a single innovation team or AI officer while the rest of the executive team watches from a distance. Every function leader needs to understand how AI changes the work their team performs, how employees will collaborate with agents and models, and where the risks are likely to appear.
That does not mean every executive needs to become a machine learning specialist, but it does mean leaders need enough fluency to guide decisions, set expectations, and model the behavior they ask of their teams. Employees are unlikely to change the way they work if their leaders treat AI as something other people are supposed to adopt.
The cultural framing also matters because if employees hear AI adoption as a euphemism for job elimination, they will protect the current version of their role rather than explore what the next version could become. Leaders should be honest that roles will change, some workflows will disappear, and new responsibilities will emerge, while also making clear that the near-term goal is to help people do higher-quality work with better leverage.
In many cases, the shift is from doing every task manually to orchestrating systems that help do the work. That requires a willingness to work through ambiguity, which becomes more important as AI becomes more capable.
The companies that succeed with AI will not be the ones that put innovation ahead of security and they will not be the ones that wait until every risk can be eliminated in advance. They will be the ones that build enough governance, verification, and data discipline to let teams move with confidence, because within enterprise AI, control is what makes speed sustainable.

articles.title: X busts 200,000-strong Chinese bot farm, including accounts making claims about AI data centers and electricity — suspect accounts posted claims about pricing and grid strain to 'manipulate' debate
articles.text:
X busts 200,000-strong Chinese bot farm, including accounts making claims about AI data centers and electricity — suspect accounts posted claims about pricing and grid strain to 'manipulate' debate
200 accounts were found posting about data centers
X’s Global Government Affairs team posted on its account that it identified a 200,000-strong bot farm operating on the platform, with 200 of them posting information designed to influence public perception. According to the team, the accounts are suspected to have been created by Chinese operators, and that they’re using the accounts to amplify the negative impacts of AI data centers, especially on electricity prices.
“We identified a bot farm of approximately 200,000 accounts. Within this farm, we found 200 accounts posting in a manner that could manipulate a legitimate debate about American AI and energy policy,” the team said in its post on the platform. “These posts contained claims that AI data centers are driving up household electricity prices and straining the grid. Others included AI-generated cartoons that depicted data-center operators enriching themselves at the public's expense.”
Some of the accounts shared by the team show names like Thomas Jackson, Patricia Robinson, Sandra Thompson, and Kenneth Flores, making it seem like they’re owned by Americans, and they’re sharing news stories from legitimate sources like The Southern Maryland Chronicle.
For example, some of their posts share the story of how PJM Interconnection hiked its prices by 76% due to AI data center demand. However, they add commentary, and sometimes even include AI-generated images designed to inflame the emotions of someone just scrolling through their feed. One narrative they’re pushing is that the costs of putting up data centers are being borne by ordinary people as big tech companies enrich themselves.
It’s unclear who sponsored or sanctioned the China-linked accounts on X, but there have been reports of China-linked operations designed to divide U.S. opinion on AI. However, the resistance against data centers isn’t all driven by Chinese propaganda, as billionaire investor Kevin O’Leary once claimed. In fact, a recent poll suggested that the biggest driver of data center protests is based on “object-level” local environmental and economic harms, especially as many other projects have shown the negative impacts they had on the community.
The concerns that many residents have about data center developments in their area are indeed valid and true, but so is the threat of foreign intervention in domestic American politics. This is no surprise, though, as nation-states have always used propaganda and information to advance their own interests. The internet, social media, and artificial intelligence have made this easier in recent years, though, so both platforms and people need to be more vigilant than ever.

articles.title: À Singapour, un rack de serveurs fonctionne avec 16 millions de neurones humains cultivés en labo
articles.text:
L’avenir de l’informatique passe-t-il par les neurones cérébraux, cultivés et développés sur des puces informatiques ? Cette image, que l’on croirait tirée tout droit de la science-fiction, est pourtant déjà très réelle. En tout cas, des travaux exploratoires sont d’ores et déjà en cours, et un prototype a même été présenté courant août, à Singapour.
Trois partenaires ont en effet dévoilé cette machine d’un genre particulier : la faculté de médecine de l’université nationale de Singapour (NUS Medicine), la startup australienne Cortical Labs et DayOne, un exploitant de centres de traitement de données (data centers). Et c’est à l’Institut des sciences de la vie de l’université que le tout a été installé.
Des unités de calcul biologiques
De quoi parle-t-on ? D’un ensemble de 20 unités de calcul biologique (« 20-unit CL1 biological computing system »). Selon les trois partenaires, il s’agit là du premier rack de serveurs au monde avec cette intégration biologique et fonctionnant de façon autonome. Et selon eux, l’enjeu d’une telle approche est avant tout énergétique.
« Contrairement aux centres de données traditionnels, qui reposent sur des serveurs très gourmands en énergie, l’informatique biologique offre un potentiel d’efficacité nettement supérieur en exploitant des organoïdes inspirés du cerveau, capables de fonctionner avec seulement une fraction de l’énergie requise par les ordinateurs numériques », relèvent-ils.
Or, à une époque où les data centers fleurissent rapidement dans le monde (sauf en France, les délais d’autorisation d’un centre dédié à l’IA se comptent en années), l’informatique biologique pourrait être une option de repli. Tout spécialement au moment où l’intelligence artificielle générative monte en puissance, et nécessite de plus en plus d’électricité.
Lors d’une précédente communication, Cortical Labs a indiqué qu’un rack complet de CL1 consomme entre 850 et 1 000 watts, là où son équivalent classique, par exemple un système Nvidia pour l’IA, pourrait réclamer 6 000 watts (les valeurs sont rapportées en watts et non en wattheures, ce qui ne dit pas s’il s’agit de l’énergie réellement consommée sur la durée).
Toujours est-il que, comme l’a relevé The Next Web, l’annonce officielle du prototype, ne contient aucun chiffre de consommation. Il n’y a pas non plus d’indication particulière dans une précédente annonce de DayOne faite au mois de mars 2026. La mention d’un wattage plus faible avait cependant été rappelée.
La comparaison énergétique laisse toutefois une question sans réponse : que calcule réellement la machine ? l’annonce ne fournit aucun test de performance non plus, ni la moindre mesure de ce que le rack accomplit par watt consommé. Sans ce chiffre, une faible consommation ne prouve pas une meilleure efficacité.
Des neurones vivants à la place des puces
Le principe sur lequel cette approche repose s’appelle le wetware. Ici, au lieu de transistors gravés dans du silicium, ces machines s’appuient sur des neurones vivants, cultivés en laboratoire à partir de cellules souches. Ceux-ci sont ensuite posés sur des grilles d’électrodes qui leur envoient et lisent des signaux électriques.
À l’heure actuelle, chaque unité CL1 de Cortical Labs contient près de 800 000 neurones, soit près de 16 millions de neurones pour les 20 unités du rack singapourien. En revanche, ces neurones ont une durée de vie limitée. Pour ce qui concerne les neurones de Cortical Labs, ceux-ci peuvent être maintenus en vie pour une durée jusqu’à six mois.
Car, effectivement, il y a une différence de taille entre les PC biologiques et leurs homologues entièrement synthétiques : les premiers ont besoin d’un système de survie incluant de l’eau, de la nourriture et des nutriments. Par ailleurs, ils génèrent aussi des déchets, et sont sensibles aux variations trop importantes de températures.
Ces enjeux sont gérés par Cortical Labs, avec une filtration des déchets et un approvisionnement. L’espérance de vie demeure un obstacle spécifique, qui pose la question (et le coût) du renouvellement des neurones. Cortical Labs avait déjà présenté une machine à neurones en 2025, au MWC de Barcelone. Mais là, on change d’échelle.
À quoi sert concrètement un tel calculateur ? Pas à remplacer un processeur : Cortical Labs positionne le CL1 comme un outil de recherche, pour la modélisation de maladies, la découverte de médicaments et l’étude du cerveau, avec l’argument d’une alternative possible aux tests sur animaux. Pour le calcul généraliste, le silicium reste incontournable.

articles.title: Biomaterials company Ponda closes crowdfunding round at €1.6 million - welcoming 256 new investors | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Ponda, a biomaterials company out of Bristol restoring wetlands through regenerative farming, has closed its latest crowdfunding campaign, raising €1.6 million (£1.4 million) in a Seed extension that welcomed 256 new investors.
The company had previously shared with EU-Startups that they were looking to raise “at least €230k (£200k), with no cap” back in April when the crowdfund was originally announced.
“Our first fibre extraction machine was a kitchen blender. Back then, we were four students experimenting with plants and an idea we couldn’t stop thinking about. Today, we are closing this crowdfunding round with a whole new community of people choosing to believe in our mission.
“A lot has happened in between, and none of it has happened alone. Ponda has been shaped by farmers, conservation groups, the paludiculture community, researchers, universities, manufacturers, brands, public funding and grant support, programmes backing deep tech startups, and the friends and families who believed in us long before any of this felt obvious,” say Julian Ellis-Brown, Nelly Tehari, Finlay Duncan and Antonia Jara, co-founders of Ponda.
Ponda’s Seed extension comes amid funding activity in European biomaterials, bio-based textiles and circular-material technologies during 2026.
EU-Startups has reported approximately €118 million across 11 comparable announcements this year, ranging from Sparxell’s €4.2 million raise for plant-based colour technology and Salt & Fiber’s €300k pre-Seed round for seagrass-based textile yarns to Syntetica’s €26.1 million Series A for nylon recycling and PaperShell’s financing of up to €40.3 million for fossil-free composites.
The UK is home several of these rounds including Epoch Biodesign’s €10.3 million financing, Naturbeads’ €4.1 million grant and Bristol-based Uplift360 and Mykor, which secured €7.4 million and €4.6 million respectively.
EU-Startups previously covered Ponda’s €2.09 million Seed round in November 2025, the launch of its crowdfunding campaign in April 2026 and a €2.76 million DEFRA-backed wetland biomaterials initiative announced in July.
“Every investment, every share and every conversation has helped strengthen our mission to restore wetlands through regenerative farming while building the next generation of4 natural performance materials,” adds the company.
Founded in 2020, Ponda is a biomaterials company developing high-performance natural fibres and insulation from wetland crops. Its first product, BioPuff, transforms bulrushes grown on restored peatlands into a renewable insulation material for apparel and outdoor products, creating a new model that combines ecosystem restoration with commercial manufacturing.
Over the past two months, Ponda has welcomed three new team members across agronomy, materials science and business development, with a further three colleagues expected to join in the coming months.
The growing team brings together expertise across farming, science, engineering and commercialisation, helping Ponda scale its network of wetland farms and develop the infrastructure needed to bring regenerative materials to market.
Behind the scenes, Ponda’s focus has remained on expanding wetland farming and strengthening its supply chain.
This summer, harvesting has taken place across wetland sites in the UK and Europe, demonstrating the potential for regenerative agriculture to produce high-performance materials at commercial scale. Ponda uses bulrush grown through paludiculture – farming on rewetted land – to create BioPuff, their plant-based insulation designed as an alternative to conventional down and synthetic insulation.
The company outlines that each harvest represents another step towards restoring degraded wetlands, supporting farmers and developing more resilient supply chains for natural materials. Healthy wetlands are also critical ecosystems for climate and biodiversity.
Peatlands are among the world’s most important carbon stores, while drained peatlands can become significant sources of greenhouse gas emissions. Rewetting and restoring these landscapes can support carbon storage, biodiversity and flood resilience while creating new opportunities for regenerative agriculture.
“Together, we have been working to connect wetland regeneration with the products people use and wear. We are incredibly grateful to every person who has played a part. With this growing community, we are one step closer to proving that better products and healthier wetlands can be part of the same future,” share the co-founders.
With the crowdfunding campaign now closed, Ponda is preparing for its next phase of
growth. Over the coming months, the company will launch new partnerships, bring more BioPuff products to market, expand its network of wetland farms and continue demonstrating how regenerative materials can reshape the future of fashion, outdoor equipment and beyond.
Ponda says the support received throughout the campaign will help accelerate this work – bringing its growing community of investors, farmers, scientists, conservationists, manufacturers and brands closer together around a shared vision for healthier wetlands and better materials.

articles.title: Shein, Temu, AliExpress : la taxe européenne sur les petits colis fait chuter les importations de 30 à 40 %
articles.text:
Un mois, c’est le temps qu’il aura fallu à la taxe européenne sur les petits colis pour commencer à mordre. Selon le ministère de l’Économie, qui s’appuie sur des chiffres des douanes françaises, les importations en provenance de Chine ont chuté de 30 à 40 % dans l’Union européenne depuis son entrée en vigueur. Du côté de certains aéroports, on parlerait même de baisses touchant la moitié du trafic habituel.
Un mécanisme simple, un volume à l’origine astronomique
Depuis le 1er juillet, une taxe de trois euros s’applique à chaque catégorie de produit contenue dans un colis importé, dès lors que sa valeur reste inférieure à 150 euros. Un colis mêlant un t-shirt, une coque de smartphone et un jouet se voit ainsi taxé trois fois, quand un colis de trois t-shirts identiques n’est taxé qu’une seule fois.
Le dispositif cible avant tout les plateformes asiatiques Shein, Temu et AliExpress, à l’origine d’un afflux de colis devenu difficile à ignorer. En 2025, près de 5,9 milliards de petits colis sont entrés sur le marché européen, soit plus de 180 chaque seconde, un volume quatre fois supérieur à celui de 2022. Sur ce total, 93 % provenaient de Chine, ces plateformes profitant jusqu’ici d’une exonération de droits de douane sur les colis de moins de 150 euros.
Des données qui convergent, un test aussi côté Royaume-Uni
Les chiffres des douanes françaises trouvent un écho du côté des données bancaires françaises. Selon l’application Joko, qui analyse les transactions de 1,5 million de personnes en France, les ventes en volume de Temu ont reculé de 50 % entre juin et juillet, celles d’AliExpress de 37 % et celles de Shein de 15 % seulement. Dans le même temps, le panier moyen a bondi de 30 % chez Temu et de 27 % chez AliExpress, signe que les acheteurs restants regroupent davantage d’articles par commande pour limiter l’impact de la taxe.
La résistance plus marquée de Shein s’expliquerait par une stratégie d’anticipation : l’entreprise a ouvert dès décembre 2025 un entrepôt de 740 000 m² en Pologne, soit l’équivalent d’une centaine de terrains de football. Les marchandises y sont stockées en gros volume avant d’être reconditionnées en petits colis puis acheminées par la route vers les clients européens, un montage qui permet d’échapper au statut de colis importé directement depuis la Chine, et donc à la taxe elle-même.
Un comparatif involontaire vient aussi conforter cette lecture globale : au Royaume-Uni, non concerné par le dispositif européen, les plateformes chinoises ont au contraire enregistré une hausse de 5 % de leurs ventes en valeur en juillet, selon l’institut NielsenIQ.
Un rebond après l’échec de la taxe française
Ce succès contraste avec l’expérience française du printemps. Paris avait tenté sa propre taxe de deux euros dès le 1er mars, avant l’entrée en vigueur du dispositif européen. Une initiative rapidement contournée : les plateformes avaient simplement redirigé leurs colis vers des pays frontaliers, notamment via l’aéroport de Liège, avant de les acheminer par la route jusqu’en France, provoquant au passage des suppressions de postes dans le fret parisien. Face à cet échec, la France avait fini par suspendre sa taxe nationale au profit du seul dispositif européen.
« Face à la Chine, il n’y a pas de fatalité », s’est félicité le ministre de l’Économie Roland Lescure lors de l’événement de rentrée du Medef. « On s’est battus il y a à peu près un an pour introduire une taxe sur les petits colis, au niveau français, ça n’a pas marché, ça a été contourné. Au niveau européen, ça devait se mettre en place en 2028 », a-t-il rappelé, revendiquant d’avoir accéléré le calendrier initialement prévu par Bruxelles.
Des critiques et une suite déjà programmée
AliExpress a réagi auprès de l’AFP en dénonçant des « failles fondamentales » dans la conception de la mesure, estimant que ces surcoûts « pèsent de manière disproportionnée sur les ménages à faibles revenus à travers l’Europe ». Shein n’a pas souhaité commenter, tandis que Temu n’avait pas réagi dans l’immédiat.
Le dispositif doit rester en vigueur jusqu’à une réforme plus large du système douanier européen, attendue dans deux ans. Il sera complété dès novembre par des frais de traitement supplémentaires, dont le montant, encore à déterminer, pourrait avoisiner deux euros par colis.

articles.title: Arnaque aux bornes de recharge : les QR codes continuent de faire des victimes en France, voici comment s’en protéger
articles.text:
Arnaque aux bornes de recharge : les QR codes continuent de faire des victimes en France, voici comment s’en protéger
Les QR codes frauduleux aux bornes de recharge sévissent toujours. Faites attention à chaque site vers lequel ils vous redirigent pour ne pas vous faire dépouiller de votre argent pour rien.
Usurper le QR code des bornes de recharge pour arnaquer est une pratique courante, prenant de l’ampleur au fur et à mesure de la démocratisation de la voiture électrique. La preuve, le centre-ville de Lyon l’a encore subi pendant des mois sur l’un de ses parkings. Découvrez comment vous en protéger efficacement à chaque recharge.
Une arnaque bien rodée aux faux QR codes frappe les bornes de recharge à Lyon
À Lyon, faire le plein d’électricité s’est transformé en véritable piège pour plusieurs conducteurs de voitures électriques. Depuis décembre dernier, un escroc recouvrait en effet les QR codes officiels des bornes LPA avec ses propres autocollants frauduleux.
Son stratagème était particulièrement trompeur : le faux code renvoyait vers une plateforme miroir usurpant le service de recharge. Seule l’extension du domaine du site web différait, affichant “.site” au lieu de “.com”. Les conducteurs validaient ainsi leur règlement sans se douter que leur argent et leurs données bancaires étaient immédiatement détournés.
Également déployée sur le parking Saint-Antoine, la combine a pris fin lorsque deux agents de sécurité ont cueilli le suspect, âgé de 27 ans, sur le fait. Ayant reconnu ses arnaques, il sera jugé en février 2027. L’enquête doit désormais chiffrer précisément le préjudice global de l’arnaque.
Comment se protéger des arnaques de ce type ?
Face à cette arnaque au faux QR code, surnommée “quishing” (contraction de QR code et phishing), il est recommandé d’adopter quelques bonnes pratiques simples lors de vos recharges afin de ne pas tomber dans le piège.
Le premier réflexe est d’inspecter visuellement et au toucher le QR code de la borne : s’il s’agit d’un autocollant superposé, ne le scannez jamais. Ne tentez pas non plus de le décoller pour scanner celui du dessous, qui pourrait être illisible ou abîmé… voire une autre arnaque. Signalez plutôt l’anomalie à l’exploitant du parking ou au service client de la borne, puis optez pour un autre moyen d’activation.
Ensuite, en cas d’ouverture d’une page web grâce à un QR code, examinez scrupuleusement l’adresse URL dans votre navigateur avant d’entrer la moindre information bancaire. L’extension exacte (se méfier d’extensions inhabituelles ou peu coûteuses comme “.site”, “.top”, “.info” ou “.xyz” au détriment des traditionnels “.fr” ou “.com”) et le protocole HTTPS sont des indicateurs capitaux à vérifier.
Dans l’idéal, privilégiez toujours le lancement de la session via l’application officielle de l’opérateur, votre badge de recharge RFID ou le terminal de paiement par carte bancaire directement intégré. Des méthodes fiables qui vous garantiront une transaction parfaitement sécurisée.

Windows 10 users have just weeks left before Nvidia ends Game Ready driver updates
articles.text:
A hot potato: An unwelcome moment is approaching for die-hard Windows 10 gamers. Nvidia's previously announced move to stop issuing new GeForce Game Ready drivers for the OS takes effect after October, limiting its support to quarterly security releases and critical bug fixes.
The cutoff comes one year after Microsoft officially retired Windows 10 on October 14, 2025. Nvidia granted the aging operating system an extra 12 months of full Game Ready and Studio Driver coverage, allowing owners of supported GeForce cards to continue receiving optimizations for new games.
Team Green says the final Windows 10-compatible Game Ready driver will arrive in October 2026, while the first release to exclude the OS is scheduled for November.
Existing drivers and games won't suddenly stop working once November arrives, but Windows 10 users will no longer receive the regular performance tuning, compatibility profiles, feature additions, and fixes accompanying major releases.
Over time, new titles may run less reliably or miss improvements available to otherwise identical Windows 11 systems.
Nvidia isn't abandoning Windows 10 entirely, at least not yet. Following the final full driver release, it plans to publish quarterly security updates through October 2029. Those should address critical vulnerabilities and serious bugs.
Just as Nvidia prepares to move away from Windows 10, Microsoft has extended its consumer Extended Security Updates program for another year. Enrolled Windows 10 PCs can now receive critical and important operating-system patches until October 12, 2027, although normal feature updates and technical support ended last year.
Maxwell, Pascal, and Volta GPUs already left the Game Ready program in October 2025 and receive critical security updates only through October 2028.
Valve's July 2026 Steam Hardware Survey shows Windows 10 on 24.8% of participating Windows PCs, compared with 75% for Windows 11. The survey isn't a complete picture of the PC market, but Statcounter shows a similar 69%/30% split.
Despite companies' best efforts to convince them to change, there are still plenty of Windows 10 users who won't move to the latest version of the OS. Hardware restrictions at a time when PCs are more expensive than ever are one factor, but surveillance, ads, account requirements, and an excess of AI features also put people off.

articles.title: The Witcher 4 Already Runs on All Target Platforms 2 Years Ahead of Launch
articles.text:
Friday, August 28th 2026
	
	
	
	
The Witcher 4 Already Runs on All Target Platforms 2 Years Ahead of Launch
As expected, there has been a lot of chatter online about The Witcher 4 since it was announced that the game was in full development at CD Projekt Red. Now, as per an interview Game Developer, CD Projekt Red's Michał Nowakowski has revealed what he meant when he said that the studio had learned from the launch of Cyberpunk 2077: The Witcher 4 already runs on all of the target systems—PlayStation 5, PC, and Xbox Series X|S.
Michał Nowakowski, co-CEO of CD Projekt RedYou come to the studio, you launch Witcher 4 right now. You can launch it on PC. You can launch it on PS5. You can launch it on Xbox Series X, and it's going to run...
The fact that The Witcher 4 already runs on all of its target systems is notable, because, as noted in our Gamescom reporting, the studio only expects to launch The Witcher 4 in 2028. 
The co-CEO explained that this is the opposite of the approach that it took with the development of Cyberpunk 2077, which was developed mainly targeting PC aiming for the highest available fidelity, and the studio had an "as it turned out, false belief that toning it down to whatever was the current gen is not going to be that much of a challenge." Nowakowski says that, since the debacle that came out of the Cyberpunk 2077 launch, "we don't take chances. We want to be sure that it actually works."
CD Projekt Red previously divulged that the Cyberpunk 2077 launch and development process also changed the way the studio kept track of systems and organization during development, and that the studio now has very strict procedures in place that ensure that institutional knowledge is spread across the teams and that everyone working on the same project has access to the same knowledge base.

articles.title: Rocket Report: Europe splashes some cash on launch startups; Pallas-1 nears debut
articles.text:
Welcome to Edition 9.08 of the Rocket Report! Some major news this week from the state of Louisiana, previously associated with space due to NASA’s aging Michoud Assembly Facility near New Orleans. Now the state has a chance to become the epicenter of SpaceX’s Starship program as the company plans to invest up to $100 billion to construct factories and multiple launch pads for the super heavy lift rocket. It would utterly transform coastal Louisiana.
As always, we welcome reader submissions, and if you don’t want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar.
ESA announces big launch challenge contracts. The European Space Agency said Thursday it signed contracts with a handful of European launch startups to help them continue development of their vehicles. “The European Launcher Challenge is ESA’s initiative to expand European launch service supply and ensure more robustness in Europe’s access to space,” the space agency said of the award, which supports the development and operation of small launch vehicles in Europe. For some of these firms, the funding will provide a key lifeline.
And the winners are … Rocket Factory Augsburg, based in Germany and developing the RFA One rocket, received 186.9 million euros and is mainly funded by Germany, with a contribution by the United Kingdom. PLD Space, based in Spain and developing the Miura 5 rocket, received 158.9 million euros and is mainly funded by Spain with a contribution by Germany. Isar Aerospace, based in Germany and developing the Spectrum launcher, received 197.8 million euros and is mainly funded by Germany, with contributions by Austria and Norway. Another contract award process with MaiaSpace is nearing completion, the agency said.
Skyroot is great, but India needs more. Jatan Mehta writes some of the most insightful articles about India’s space program, and we wanted to highlight his six-part series on what he calls “India’s launch vehicle crisis.” Part six of this series was published on Sunday, and it explains why, despite the recent success of Skyroot and its Vikram-1 rocket, India’s growing gap in orbital launch capacity will remain unresolved. “Even if we hope and assume that the thousand-plus people of Skyroot bag a commendable place in the small-lift launch market, that does not in itself solve India’s space access crisis,” Mehta writes.
India’s government needs to be proactive … He notes that the country faces major constraints in spaceports, suppliers, and especially medium- and heavy-lift rockets. “Skyroot’s success with the first flight of Vikram-1 is only the least worst case scenario for India’s launch vehicle crisis,” Mehta says. “It’s not at the peak alongside people’s emotions but at the bare minimum level to cater to but a fraction of India’s needs in space.”
The Ars Technica Rocket Report
The easiest way to keep up with Eric Berger’s and Stephen Clark’s reporting on all things space is to sign up for our newsletter. We’ll collect their stories and deliver them straight to your inbox.
Japanese startup wins launch contract. A Japanese radar-imaging startup has signed an agreement to launch its first demonstration satellite on Space One’s Kairos rocket, Space News reports. Space One and Sarmony announced on August 25 that they signed a memorandum of understanding regarding the launch of Sarmony’s first SAR DiskSat spacecraft on a Kairos rocket in 2028.
A bold choice … Kairos has launched three times to date, in each case failing to reach orbit. On the most recent launch in March, the vehicle broke apart a little more than a minute after liftoff. A Space One representative said the company is completing the investigation into the failure and plans to release more details soon. The company has not announced a schedule for the next Kairos launch.
Falcon 9 Starlink launches from Florida end. It’s the end of an era in Florida, Ars reports. A Falcon 9 launch early Tuesday was the last planned Starlink mission from Cape Canaveral until SpaceX begins flying Starship missions from Florida, according to Kiko Dontchev, the company’s vice president of launch. “From here on, Starlink missions out of Florida will fly on Starship,” Dontchev said. “The West Coast team will continue regularly launching Starlink from Vandenberg.”
A real workhorse … SpaceX launched around 260 Starlink missions on Falcon 9 from Florida, but all future Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy launches from Florida will carry external customer payloads. The next one is scheduled for August 30, when a Falcon Heavy rocket will lift off from Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy Space Center with NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Officials eventually plan to phase out the Falcon 9 in favor of Starship, at least for commercial missions, raising concerns among SpaceX customers about the availability of reliable launch services after 2028.
Pallas-1 rocket nears debut. Chinese commercial firm Galactic Energy is ready for a first orbital launch attempt with its Pallas-1 liquid propellant launch vehicle, Space News reports. Newly published airspace warnings now indicate a launch window of between 9:52 pm ET on August 31 and 12:09 am ET on September 1 (01:52–04:09 UTC, September 1). While the rocket is designed for reusability, no recovery attempt of the first stage is expected for the first flight. No payloads have so far been announced ahead of launch.
Solidly a medium-lift vehicle … Pallas-1 is Galactic Energy’s two-stage liquid launch vehicle, with an optional Eros upper stage for extended missions. It has a 3.35 meter-diameter body, a 4.2 meter-diameter fairing, a liftoff mass of 283 tons, and liftoff thrust of 350 tons, according to Galactic Energy’s webpages. While payload capacity stats have fluctuated during development, the firm states a maximum payload capacity of 7,000 kilograms to low-Earth orbit.
New federal policy calls for additional spaceports. A new national space transportation policy signed by President Donald Trump calls for the development of more spaceports to support more than 1,000 launches and reentries per year by 2030, Ars reports. The most notable updates to the national space transportation policy focus on increasing the country’s ability to enable those lofty forecasts. The Trump administration calls on the Pentagon and NASA to “prioritize and coordinate on infrastructure investments” to boost launch and reentry capacity and flexibility at federal launch and reentry ranges.
Finding additional launch facilities … The policy document supports more efficient range scheduling criteria at federally owned spaceports, balancing the needs of commercial users and US government missions. It also directs the military and NASA to “regularly publish range schedules to ensure transparent allocation of resources and optimize launch capacity.” Today, the schedules for most rocket launches are not public until a few days or weeks in advance. The government will also identify potential locations for additional launch facilities in the United States, improve integration of space launch and reentry operations into airspace and air traffic control modernization efforts, and designate “priority airspace for critical space launch corridors.”
Ariane 6 set for first geostationary launch. On Thursday, Arianespace is scheduled to launch the MTG-I2 meteorological satellite with the Ariane 62 configuration from Europe’s Spaceport in French Guiana. According to Arianespace, the MTG-I2 mission will mark the fourth Ariane 6 launch of the year and the rocket’s first to a geostationary orbit.
Flying high, for now … In addition to these milestones, this will be the ninth overall launch by the Ariane 6 program, which was developed by the European Space Agency and is now operated by Arianespace. From a technical standpoint, Europe’s workhorse rocket continues to perform well, but there are questions about its long-term viability.
SpaceX plans massive Starship launch site in Louisiana. Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry said Tuesday that SpaceX will commit $100 billion to develop Starship factories and launch pads in the state’s coastal areas. In doing so, the company seeks to replicate the Starbase facility it has built over the last decade in southern Texas on a larger scale, Ars reports. Gwynne Shotwell, the president and chief operating officer of SpaceX, said the “Starbase Louisiana” facility would become a self-sustaining spaceport with propellant production, power generation, deep-water shipping capabilities, vehicle processing facilities, and an airport on site.
It will be much larger in scale … The Starbase Texas site encompasses only about 350 acres, and SpaceX also must maintain public access to Boca Chica Beach as much as possible along a single roadway. By contrast, SpaceX is expected to have unfettered access to about 125,000 acres in southern Louisiana, in an area generally referred to as Pecan Island. SpaceX plans to begin construction of the first launch facilities in 2027 and is targeting an initial launch from Louisiana by 2029. Eventually, the company may build as many as a dozen Starship launch towers at the location.
China delays key lunar launch. China’s “Manned Space” program issued a terse announcement on Sunday regarding its much-anticipated Chang’e 7 lunar exploration mission, Ars reports. The agency stated: “In keeping with the principle of proceeding prudently and reliably, and ensuring absolute success, after a comprehensive assessment it has been determined that the Chang’e 7 mission does not meet the conditions for launch and therefore cannot be carried out during the planned launch window this year.”
A key step in the race back to the Moon … Consisting of a lunar orbiter, lander, rover, and a mini-hopper probe, the mission was due to launch as early as Sunday on a Long March 5 rocket. It is intended to land at the south pole of the Moon. Although official Chinese sources have provided no confirmed information, there has been social media chatter indicating that another suitable launch window may not open until next February or March. Why so long? It’s likely a combination of factors, including sunlight conditions in polar landing zones and the mission plan, which requires a 90-day lunar orbit reconnaissance before landing.
Nearly time for Roman to fly. NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope arrived Tuesday at the SpaceX hangar at Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, just days before its scheduled liftoff on a Falcon Heavy rocket, the US space agency said. NASA, Roman, and SpaceX teams will host a Launch Readiness Review on Friday to conduct the final “go/no go” poll ahead of the planned 7:26 am ET launch on August 30, from Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy.
A far-seeing instrument … Launching nine months ahead of schedule, Roman is expected to transform the way we see the Universe and settle essential questions about some of the biggest mysteries out there. Roman has a wide field of view that will rapidly capture huge swaths of sky full of stars and galaxies once it reaches the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point 2, or L2.
Next three launches
August 27: Ariane 6 | MTG-I2 | Guiana Space Centre, French Guiana | 20:10 UTC
August 30: Falcon Heavy | Roman Space Telescope | Kennedy Space Center, Florida | 11:25 UTC
August 31: Electron | Own Around the World | Māhia Peninsula, New Zealand | 12:05 UTC
Eric Berger is the senior space editor at Ars Technica, covering everything from astronomy to private space to NASA policy, and author of two books: Liftoff, about the rise of SpaceX; and Reentry, on the development of the Falcon 9 rocket and Dragon. A certified meteorologist, Eric lives in Houston.

articles.title: Google cambia las reglas con Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM), que estrena nuevos límites
articles.text:
Si eres un ávido usuario de Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM), muy pronto comenzarás a ver un cambio muy importante. Google ha decidido dotar a sus cuadernos de IA con nuevos límites de uso basados en el consumo de poder de cómputo, idénticos a los que meses atrás implementó en la app de Gemini.
Según los de Mountain View, la modificación busca darle mayor flexibilidad a los usuarios de Gemini Notebook. La compañía sostiene que los límites ya no son diarios, sino que se renuevan cada cinco horas. Esto permite seguir trabajando durante la misma jornada, sin tener que esperar hasta el día siguiente para recuperar determinadas funcionalidades.
Hasta aquí, Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM) permitía un número fijo de generaciones en el transcurso del día. Esto dependía el tipo de cuenta o plan de IA contratado por el usuario. En adelante, la plataforma implementará una doble barrera de tiempo. ¿Esto qué significa? Que por un lado estarán los límites de uso que se renovarán cada cinco horas, mientras por otro estará el tope semanal.
"Los límites de uso de Gemini Notebook están diseñados para garantizar una experiencia óptima para todos. Esto significa que, en ocasiones, es posible que tengamos que limitar la cantidad de mensajes y conversaciones que puedes tener, o el uso de ciertas funciones, dentro de un período de tiempo determinado", menciona la empresa.
Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM) introduce nuevos límites de uso
Los nuevos límites de Gemini Notebook comenzarán a regir el próximo 2 de septiembre y se apoyarán en diferentes parámetros. Esto quiere decir que el consumo de los límites disponibles se verá impactado por factores como la complejidad del prompt y la tarea a realizar, la cantidad de funciones y fuentes que se usen, o la duración del chat. Ten en cuenta que si trabajas continuamente sobre un chat preexistente, la plataforma debe cargar todo el contexto previo y eso lleva a que los límites se alcancen más rápido.
Google menciona que Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM) ofrecerá advertencias cuando se esté por alcanzar un límite de uso, como también al acabar el cómputo disponible. Lo interesante es que la plataforma no siempre restringirá el acceso a las funciones cuando se llegue al límite. En ciertos casos, ofrecerá funciones alternativas para salir del paso. Asimismo, introducirá una opción de "generar más tarde" para que ciertas tareas se puedan completar de forma automática al renovarse la cuota disponible.
Si bien Google habla de brindar más flexibilidad a los usuarios de Gemini Notebook, los cambios en los límites de uso también buscan seducir a potenciales nuevos suscriptores de sus planes de pago. La compañía menciona que los usuarios de Google AI Plus tienen el doble del límite que quienes usan la versión gratuita, mientras que en Google AI Pro son cuatro veces más altos. En el caso de Google AI Ultra, son entre 5 y 20 veces mayores que los del plan previo.

articles.title: Google further buries search results under AI mode
articles.text:
Google is now automatically expanding its AI search summaries at the top of the results page for some searches, as reported by Search Engine Roundtable. The change, when it kicks in, pushes the typical list of links from a search much farther down Google’s results page; instead of seeing part of an AI Overview with a “Show more” button you can click, you’ll Google will show a full AI Overview at the top of your search, an “Ask anything” box under that, and then the list of links. It can lead to a lot of scrolling.
Google further buries search results under AI mode
Google now automatically expands its AI search summaries for some queries.
It’s unclear exactly what Google’s criteria is for the auto-expanding AI Overviews. Before writing this story, I was seeing them with most of my test searches. But now, AI Overviews usually just show the initial part of the response and the “Show more” button. My most consistent query to get the auto-expanding AI Overview is “what is the best game on switch 2”, but even that hasn’t been consistent across searches and browsers.
“For some queries, AI Overviews may dynamically expand for topics where our systems determine it’s most useful for people,” Google spokesperson Jennifer Kutz says in a statement to The Verge. “Our research has shown that with this dynamic experience, users find Search more helpful and engage deeper in follow-up exploration.” Kutz also says that “If users have already begun scrolling to view content below the AI Overview, we cancel expansion so that the user doesn’t lose their reading position.”

articles.title: The Download: a secretive antiaging drug and joining virtual power plants
articles.text:
The Download: a secretive antiaging drug and joining virtual power plants
Plus: A judge has blocked the Pentagon’s blacklisting of Anthropic.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
A startup claims it’s found a drug to make your blood young
—Antonio Regalado
I knew I’d officially become a “longevity influencer” when a company called Generation Lab offered me the chance to write about—and even receive—their new rejuvenation treatment.
This wasn’t just any antiaging treatment, either. A company fact sheet says that it “blocks the systemic spread of aging in the bloodstream, reawakens the body’s own repair mechanism and restores health and youth to multiple tissues.”
The approach is based on research by Generation Lab’s irascible scientific founder, Irina Conboy. She found that joining the circulatory systems of old and young mice improved the old animals’ ability to heal from injury.
Conboy now says she has found a combination of two existing drugs that can produce youthful effects without the need for any bodily fluid exchange. But Generation Lab won’t reveal what the drugs are, making the proposition hard to take seriously.
Read the full story on the drug combo that claims to “stop the spread of aging.”
How to sign up for a virtual power plant—and decide whether you should
Your thermostat may not look like a power plant. Neither does your electric vehicle, home battery, or HVAC system. But utility and energy companies increasingly want to treat them like one.
That’s the idea behind a virtual power plant, or VPP, a collection of household devices (such as smart thermostats, EV chargers, and solar panels) that a utility can control, usually by commanding them to draw less electricity during peak hours. In exchange, participants receive a discount on their energy bills and, in some cases, a signing bonus.
Here’s how to sign up for a VPP—and decide whether it’s worth it.
—Eshan Raul
This story is part of MIT Technology Review’s How To series, which gives you practical advice on getting things done. Check out the rest of the series here.
The must-reads
I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.
1 A judge has blocked the Pentagon’s blacklisting of Anthropic
The court found the designation violated First Amendment rights. (NYT $)
+ And ruled that the designation was based on retaliation. (CNBC) 
+ Anthropic still faces a separate case in Washington, DC. (Reuters $)
+ The Pentagon’s culture war against Anthropic backfired. (MIT Technology Review)
2 Tech giants have called for a defensive surge to defeat AI-driven hacks
Over 100 companies warned that a wave of cyberattacks is imminent. (BBC)
+ And urged government and industry leaders to take rapid action. (Quartz)
+ Their main solution, unsurprisingly, is more AI. (Gizmodo)
+ Here’s why OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face. (MIT Technology Review)
3 Anthropic has launched an AI tool that conducts scientific experiments
It lets AI agents autonomously operate microscopes, lasers, and robotic arms. (FT $)
+ And includes rules designed for safe operations in labs. (Wired $)
+ It’s Anthropic’s first tool designed for the physical world. (Ars Technica)
4 India’s data center boom is leaving the people it displaces with nothing
Policymakers courting Big Tech are sidelining local communities. (Rest of World)
+ No one wants a data center in their backyard. (MIT Technology Review)
5 OpenAI is testing a “persistent” AI agent that keeps working
Codex could continue tasks until it’s “put to sleep.” (Wired $)
+ And generate follow-up tasks without prompting. (Gizmodo)
6 A lawsuit alleges that Grok was trained on child sexual abuse material
It claims victims’ images entered the chatbot’s training data. (Ars Technica)
+ A federal judge says AI has outpaced child-abuse laws. (WP $)
7 AI writing has reached a turning point in the media
Sparked by the Wall Street Journal defending an AI-written op-ed. (Atlantic $)
8 China’s robotic racers are exposing the limits of human speed
Their advances are revealing what our bodies can’t do. (Reuters $)
9 Young workers are turning to “AI-proof” traditional crafts
They’re drawn to creative, hands-on skills that tech can’t easily replicate. (Guardian)
10 Scientists have a new army to fight invasive crabs: 150,000 baby octopuses
Italian researchers just released the animals into the Adriatic Sea. (New Scientist $)
Quote of the day
“The academic record is being quietly haunted.”
—A new preprint research paper from Samsung and the University of Warsaw warns that a torrent of AI-generated study papers written by fake researchers is contaminating academic publishing.
One more thing
The problem with thinking you’re part Neanderthal
There’s a theory that many of us have an “inner Neanderthal.” The idea is that Homo sapiens and a cousin species once bred, leaving some people today with a trace of Neanderthal DNA.
This DNA is arguably the 21st century’s most celebrated discovery in human evolution. But in 2024, a pair of French geneticists called into question the theory’s very foundations.
They proposed that what scientists interpret as interbreeding could instead be explained by population structure—the way genes concentrate in smaller, isolated groups.
Find out what it all means for human evolution.
—Ben Crair
We can still have nice things
A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line.)

+ Bowerbirds in Australia are turning human trash into treasure to impress females.

articles.title: Anthropic replica la jugada de OpenAI: quiere su propio chip de IA para reducir su dependencia de Nvidia
articles.text:
A las empresas que se dedican al desarrollo de modelos de inteligencia artificial (IA) les interesa tener sus propios chips para entrenamiento e inferencia. Google tiene sus TPU (Tensor Processing Unit) 8t y 8i, ambas de última generación. Meta, su familia de aceleradores MTIA (Meta Training and Inference Accelerator), con el recién presentado MTIA 300 a la cabeza. Y OpenAI tiene su chip Jalapeño, recién lanzado y optimizado para tareas de inferencia.
Amazon y Microsoft también han desarrollado sus propios aceleradores para IA, pero hay otra compañía que ha decidido recorrer este camino, y merece la pena que le sigamos la pista muy de cerca: Anthropic. A la compañía liderada por Dario Amodei le interesa tener sus propios chips por dos motivos. El más evidente no es otro que reducir su dependencia de las GPU de Nvidia, que tienen un coste muy alto y su disponibilidad oscila mucho debido a las dificultades que tiene TSMC, que es la empresa que las fabrica, a la hora de dar respuesta a la demanda.
La otra razón que tiene Anthropic para desarrollar sus propios aceleradores para IA consiste en que controlar la fase de diseño de la lógica de estos chips le permitiría optimizarlos para entrenar sus propios modelos de la familia Claude y resolver sus cada vez mayores necesidades de inferencia. No obstante, este proyecto no es un camino de rosas. Diseñar circuitos integrados es caro y lento, sobre todo cuando partes de cero. De hecho, desarrollar una sola generación de aceleradores de IA suele tener unos costes de varios cientos de millones de dólares. Sea como sea, aquí es donde aparece la segunda protagonista de esta historia: MatX.
A la caza y captura de un socio
Anthropic no quiere partir de cero. Y para sortear este obstáculo la mejor opción es bien comprar una empresa especializada en el diseño de chips para IA, bien asociarse con ella si la adquisición no es posible. Es justo lo que están haciendo los creadores de Claude. Y es que, según Reuters, Anthropic ha estado explorando la posibilidad de comprar MatX, una empresa emergente estadounidense de diseño de chips, por unos 7.000 millones de dólares. No obstante, como podemos intuir, esta no es una firma cualquiera que diseña circuitos integrados.
MatX fue fundada en 2022 por Reiner Pope y Mike Gunter, dos exingenieros de Google
MatX fue fundada en 2022 por Reiner Pope y Mike Gunter, dos exingenieros de Google que participaron en el desarrollo de su familia de TPU. Pope es experto en el desarrollo de software e infraestructura para modelos de lenguaje, y Gunter tiene mucha experiencia en el diseño de la lógica de los aceleradores de IA. Su complementariedad es perfecta. Según Reuters, la intención inicial de Anthropic era comprar MatX, pero la negociación ha derivado finalmente hacia un acuerdo de asociación que, al parecer, todavía no se ha consolidado.
Actualmente los ingenieros de MatX están diseñando un acelerador optimizado específicamente para el entrenamiento de los modelos de IA, mientras que tanto sus competidores como la mayor parte de las compañías que desarrollan los modelos están volcados con la inferencia. Esta diferenciación probablemente ha llamado la atención de Anthropic, que, no obstante, necesita tanto chips optimizados para el entrenamiento como para la inferencia.
Prospere o no su acuerdo con MatX, hay un hecho irrefutable: Dario Amodei y los suyos quieren tener sus propios chips. De lo contrario no habrían fichado esta misma semana a Amir Salek, un veterano del diseño de chips que salió de Google en 2022 y desde entonces ha trabajado para Cerberus Capital Management.

articles.title: More Americans oppose police license plate cameras than support them: survey | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The growing backlash against surveillance companies like Flock may have reached a tipping point. A new survey has found that more Americans oppose these surveillance cameras than support them.
According to a new YouGov survey of 20,000 people across the U.S. that was shared exclusively with The Washington Post, 46% of respondents opposed the company’s surveillance cameras in their communities, while 38% supported them. This is a reversal from last year, when the majority of survey respondents said they were in favor.
Flock is one of the more visible surveillance companies, operating more than 120,000 license plate readers across the U.S. that can track the whereabouts of vehicles. The company has been embroiled in controversy following reports of police abusing the cameras’ surveillance, which resulted in dozens of U.S. communities rejecting Flock’s cameras or canceling their contracts amid privacy concerns.
The survey also reported that more respondents said the surveillance would not make them feel any safer.
When reached by TechCrunch, Flock claimed there was wide support for its surveillance technology, but acknowledged that “support isn’t unconditional,” and touted the rollout of its recent safeguards. Critics, like the ACLU, have said the company’s new safeguards amount to little, and Flock remains a major threat to civil liberties.
Amid the intensifying backlash, Flock CEO Garrett Langley last week called for a “compromise” between surveillance and privacy, following a rise in vandalism targeting Flock cameras.

articles.title: 'The performance, for now, is 30fps' — GTA 6 will run at 30fps on console, but higher performance modes could reportedly arrive post-launch
articles.text:
GTA 6 will launch at 30fps on PS5 and Xbox 'for now', confirms Rockstar — but while 60fps is reportedly possible, it's a 40fps mode we really want to see
The GTA 6 Extended Look footage was running at 30fps
- Grand Theft Auto 6 will launch at 30fps on PS5, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S
- Rockstar could reportedly add higher performance modes post-launch
- The footage from the GTA 6 Extended Look was running on the base PS5, which means everything fans saw was 30fps
Grand Theft Auto 6 won't run at 60fps and will reportedly launch at 30fps on consoles, but Rockstar Games may add more performance modes later.
That's according to YouTuber Davy Jones, a content creator who recently visited Rockstar North to preview GTA 6. Jones reported that Rob Nelson, the head of development and co-studio head at Rockstar North, told him the game is currently running at 30fps on console during development.
Flow Games also interviewed Jones about his time at the studio (translated via Kotaku) and reported that performance could change post-launch.
"According to Rob Nelson, Lead Developer and Co-director at Rockstar North, during this development period, the consoles are running the game at 30 frames per second," the Flow Gams report reads.
"According to the director, it is still necessary to consult the technical team to determine if there will be a 60 FPS option at launch (or in the future). He also emphasizes that he does not currently have details on resolution and other technical qualities, such as the use of Ray Tracing, but the performance, for now, is 30 FPS."
For now, Rockstar also hasn't confirmed whether the game will run at 60fps on PS5 Pro.
Last night, the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look finally premiered and offered a deep dive into gameplay, cinematics, and co-protagonists Jason and Lucia.

The footage looks incredible and was confirmed to be running on the base PS5, and knowing what we do now, this means the extended look was also capped at 30fps.
